title: Elon Musk Dismisses $120B Anthropic Exit Talk as SpaceX Plans $74B AI Push
summary: SpaceX unveiled plans to invest more than $74 billion in artificial intelligence computing facilities as Elon Musk dismissed speculation about Anthropic abandoning a $120.5 billion agreement. The expansion comes as AI yielded more than half of SpaceX’s third-quarter revenue, with the Anthropic deal ...
content:
SpaceX unveiled plans to invest more than $74 billion in artificial intelligence computing facilities as Elon Musk dismissed speculation about Anthropic abandoning a $120.5 billion agreement. The expansion comes as AI yielded more than half of SpaceX’s third-quarter revenue, with the Anthropic deal accounting for a substantial share.

Key Takeaways

  • SpaceX plans more than $74 billion in Texas and Arizona AI facilities.
  • The firm’s Super Intelligence segment generated 52% of its quarterly revenue.
  • Anthropic reportedly accounted for 34.5% of SpaceX’s quarterly revenue.

Musk’s $74 Billion AI Expansion Targets Texas and Arizona

Elon Musk’s SpaceX (Nasdaq: SPCX) announced plans on Nov. 12 to invest more than $74 billion in two AI supercomputing facilities in Texas and Arizona. The expansion followed Musk’s response to speculation about Anthropic’s $120.5 billion computing agreement, linking the company’s ambitious spending plans to questions about future customer demand.

SpaceX outlined its planned computing expansion, allocating more than $24 billion to its Starbase facility in Texas and approximately $50 billion to a proposed campus in Cochise County, Arizona. The Texas project will generate its own electricity rather than rely on the public grid. The company expects more than 500 permanent jobs there, while the Arizona development could create approximately 1,000 permanent positions.

The proposed Arizona facility faces regulatory and safety challenges. Cochise County’s development application describes a 747-acre site with up to nine computing buildings and an estimated electricity demand of 6 gigawatts at full capacity. The project requires county approval and has drawn public opposition.

At a Nov. 12 meeting, the county’s Local Emergency Planning Committee reportedly approved six recommendations addressing fire protection, battery storage, and emergency response capabilities. The advisory panel sought stronger safeguards before development proceeds.

One Customer Accounted for 34.5% of SpaceX’s Quarterly Revenue

The multibillion-dollar investment plans come as SpaceX’s AI operations account for a growing share of its business. Its third-quarter SEC filing showed that the Super Intelligence segment generated $7.56 billion, approximately 52% of total quarterly revenue of $14.58 billion. The segment, which includes computing services, software, and advertising, reported $431 million in operating income, reversing a $1.72 billion loss a year earlier.

Much of that revenue is concentrated among major customers. Bloomberg identified Anthropic as SpaceX’s largest customer, citing a person familiar with the relationship. SpaceX disclosed that a single customer, labeled Customer B, accounted for 34.5% of third-quarter revenue.

That reliance has attracted scrutiny following unverified claims that Anthropic could decline to extend its computing agreement beyond mid-2027. Responding to speculation surrounding the agreement on Nov. 11, Musk stated on X:

“We would be happy to take the compute back. No problem. But I think the opposite is going to happen.”

The speculation emerged as Anthropic prepared for a major initial public offering (IPO). Its Nov. 10 filing proposed selling 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, representing a potential offering of $57.75 billion to $64.35 billion before underwriting fees. The company applied to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, subject to completion of the offering.

Anthropic’s amended Securities and Exchange Commission filing, submitted Nov. 10, detailed computing agreements with SpaceX.AI LLC worth up to $120.5 billion over terms extending into 2029. Monthly payments are expected to reach approximately $3.1 billion once all contracted capacity becomes available, currently anticipated in December. Either company can terminate the relevant agreements with 90 days’ written notice after initial noncancelable periods expire in January and March 2027.

Massive AI Investments Face Competing Demand Expectations

The expansion and Anthropic agreement reflect SpaceX’s bet on sustained demand for AI computing power. Musk previously defended SpaceX’s long-term ambitions amid criticism of its AI computing arrangements. Venture capitalist Chamath Palihapitiya suggested constrained supplies could strengthen the company’s negotiating position, while Musk acknowledged that cheaper, more abundant capacity could reduce revenue.

Anthropic also maintains substantial computing relationships with Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and other providers. Beyond these centralized suppliers, decentralized AI computing networks offer an alternative model that distributes processing capacity among independent operators. Such networks remain distinct from the large corporate facilities supporting Anthropic’s agreements.

SpaceX is separately pursuing Musk’s plans for space-based AI computing, including orbital data centers designed to operate beyond terrestrial infrastructure. The company faces two significant tests: whether customers continue purchasing sufficient computing capacity and whether its proposed facilities secure regulatory approvals. The Arizona project faces its next review on Dec. 9, when county officials will consider the development amid public opposition and emergency preparedness concerns.

title: MEXC Exchange Review: Is It Safe & Legit in 2026?

MEXC is a global crypto exchange with very low trading fees, more than 3,000 listed digital assets, and high-leverage futures, but it is not licensed or available in every country.

It serves over 40 million users across more than 170 countries. Still, people in the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, and several other blocked regions cannot open or use an account.

In this MEXC review, we will cover its fees, supported coins, futures trading, security features, KYC rules, and withdrawal process. You will also learn whether MEXC is safe in your country, who should use it, and which alternatives may suit you better.

What Is MEXC Global Crypto Exchange?

MEXC is a centralized crypto exchange that lets you buy, sell, hold, and trade digital assets from one account. The platform was launched back in 2018 under the name MXC Exchange, then rebranded to MEXC a couple of years later, and it has grown fast ever since.

You get access to spot markets, leveraged futures, savings products, and even a stock-trading arm called RealStocks, all inside one app or website. MEXC mainly built its name around altcoins. It lists new tokens faster than most big-name exchanges.

Now, below is a quick snapshot to give you a first glance at what MEXC actually offers:

Founded2018
Exchange TypeCentralized crypto exchange
User Reach40+ million users; 170+ markets claimed
Supported Coins3,000+ cryptocurrencies
Spot Fees0% maker; 0.05% taker
Futures Fees0% maker; 0.02% taker
Trading FeaturesSpot, futures, trading bots, copy trading, and P2P
Maximum LeverageUp to 200x in eligible regions
Withdrawal LimitsPrimary KYC: 80 BTC; Advanced KYC: 200 BTC daily
Crypto DepositsFree
Fiat OptionsCards, P2P, and third-party providers
Security Tools2FA, passkeys, anti-phishing code, withdrawal whitelist
Restricted RegionsUS, UK, Canada, China, Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, Kazakhstan, and others

What Are the Pros of MEXC?

The pros of MEXC are low trading fees, 3,000+ supported coins, copy trading, built-in bots, advanced futures tools, and published Proof of Reserves.

  • Zero-fee spot maker orders: You pay 0% on maker orders and just 0.05% on taker orders, well below the industry average.
  • Huge coin selection: You can find more than 3,000 crypto coins on MEXC. It has top coins like Bitcoin, but it also has low-cap tokens that you will not find on other platforms.
  • No mandatory KYC for basic use: You can sign up, deposit crypto, and trade spot or futures without submitting ID, at least up to a daily withdrawal limit (limits and no-KYC availability depend on region).
  • Copy trading and bots: The platform includes copy trading, grid bots, and DCA tools built right into the interface.
  • Advanced tools for futures: You get high leverage, hedge mode, cross or isolated margin, trailing stops, demo trading, and bots. Even BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT can reach 200x leverage in some eligible regions.
  • Proof of reserves: MEXC publishes reserve ratios that generally sit well above 100% for major assets like BTC, ETH, and USDT.

What Are the Cons of MEXC?

The cons of MEXC are limited regulatory approval, no direct bank withdrawals in most regions, possible risk-control freezes, third-party fiat services, and thin liquidity on some smaller coins.

  • No license in major markets: MEXC does not have approval from the SEC in the US, the FCA in the UK, or a MiCA license in Europe. Because of these missing licenses, nowadays, the platform completely blocks users from the US, UK, and Canada.
  • No direct bank withdrawal: You cannot send fiat straight to your bank account from MEXC in most regions, so cashing out takes an extra step through P2P or even a second exchange.
  • Risk-control freezes: Actually, some users report accounts getting locked for identity or fund-source review, which can hold up withdrawals for days.
  • Limited fiat on-ramps: Mostly, direct card and bank deposits go through third-party providers like Banxa, MoonPay, and Mercuryo rather than MEXC itself in many regions.
  • Thin liquidity on smaller listings: Some of the newest altcoins carry very thin order books, so a bigger order can easily move the price more than you would expect.

What Are the Fees on MEXC?

MEXC charges basic trading fees of 0% maker and 0.05% taker for spot trading, plus 0% maker and 0.02% taker for futures. Crypto deposits are completely free, while withdrawal fees can easily vary by coin and network, and some trading pairs may have different rates (based on active campaigns).

Spot Trading Fees

MEXC charges 0% in spot maker fees and 0.05% in spot taker fees for standard accounts. A maker order is the one that sits on the order book and waits to get filled, while a taker order is the one that matches instantly against an existing order. MX token holders receive a 20% fee reduction, and discounts apply to eligible spot trades as well.

Futures Trading Fees

MEXC charges a 0% futures maker fee and around 0.02% taker fees for futures trades. This rate can change a little bit based on the contract and where you live, and high volume traders may qualify for better pricing through tiered programs where available in their region. Also, funding rates settle every 8 hours on most pairs, and it usually range between 0.01% and 0.03%, either positive or negative.

Deposit & Withdrawal Fees

You do not have to pay any deposit fee when you add crypto to MEXC, no matter the coin or network. For crypto withdrawals, the fee depends on the specific coin and network you pick, and it goes up or down based on network traffic.

Fiat deposits and fiat purchases usually rely on third-party providers and can vary by region, provider fees, and processing times.

Well, a USDT withdrawal on the Tron network, for example, usually costs (1 USDT fee) far less than the same withdrawal on the Ethereum network (2-5 USDT fee), so picking the right chain easily saves you real money.

Are the Trading Fees on MEXC High?

No, MEXC’s trading fees rank among the lowest in the entire crypto exchange industry. A 0% maker fee on both spot and futures markets beats what Binance, Coinbase, and most other big platforms charge by default. Even the 0.05% spot taker fee and 0.02% futures taker fee sit well under typical industry averages, which often run close to double those numbers. Claims about zero fees mainly refer to maker pricing and occasional exchange promotions, not every trade type.

How to Reduce the MEXC Trading Fees?

You can reduce your MEXC fees in several ways, and the easiest one is simply placing limit orders instead of market orders. Limit orders count as maker orders most of the time, and maker orders cost 0% on both spot and futures. You can also use the MX token to reduce fees by 20% and use our referral code “mexc-bestbonus” to further reduce fees by 10%.

MX Token Fee Discounts

MX is MEXC’s native token, and mx token holders get a direct discount on trading fees. You get a 20% discount on spot and futures fees once the required MX balance is met, and discounts apply automatically with no extra step needed beyond holding the token.

Quick Note: MEXC suspended its older 50% fee discount for holding at least 500 MX. It is temporarily suspended.

MEXC Referral Code

The MEXC referral code “mexc-bestbonus” gives a new eligible user up to a 10% trading-fee discount and access to welcome tasks worth up to 10,000 USDT. You must enter the code while creating the account.

But remember, the full 10,000 USDT is not free cash. Actually, it requires KYC, deposit, and trading-volume tasks, and larger futures rewards usually come as credit you cannot withdraw directly. You can only withdraw profits.

Is MEXC Safe and Legit Globally?

Yes, MEXC is a safe and legit exchange that serves 40 million real traders, but “legit” here does not mean “fully regulated everywhere”. The platform runs real security infrastructure, publishes proof-of-reserves data, and has operated without a major hack since 2018. Still, it holds no top-tier license in the US, the UK, or under the EU’s MiCA framework, so your legal protection depends heavily on where you live.

Basically, MEXC is safe in the technical sense, meaning your funds face reasonable protection from hackers, but it is not “safe” in the regulatory sense the way a bank-backed or fully licensed exchange would be.

Also, there have been complaints about MEXC locking user funds through its risk control system. These freezes are mostly due to abnormal cryptocurrency trading activity in the user’s account.

Regulatory Status

MEXC does not hold any worldwide license that makes every service legal across 170+ markets. In fact, it is a highly unregulated exchange and operates without any license.

Note: MEXC also says it is registered with AUSTRAC in Australia, and in Europe, the exchange uses a local company called MEXC Estonia OÜ to handle some of its legal and compliance work. But again, we could not independently verify these claims, and it seems they are either false or the license is still pending.

Also, the exchange does not have a MiCA license in the EU. The rule deadline was July 1, 2026, so platforms without a license have to get approved or stop taking EU users. Because of this, things are still changing, and we still have to wait and see if people in Europe can use it.

MEXC is currently not available in the US, UK, Canada, Singapore, Malaysia, Hong Kong, Mainland China, Iran, North Korea, Cuba, Sudan, Kazakhstan, Russian-controlled parts of Ukraine, and high-risk areas. Plus, hiding your location can lead to account closure and forced liquidation.

So, is MEXC legit? Yes, it is a real exchange. Is it fully regulated globally? No. The difference between those two answers is important.

Available Security Features

MEXC’s available account security features are 2FA, passkeys, anti-phishing code, withdrawal address whitelist, and manual temporary account freeze.

  • Google Authenticator (2FA): You can link Google Authenticator to generate a new six-digit security code every 30 seconds, even without an internet connection. Generally, MEXC uses it as an extra check for sensitive actions such as logging in, trading, and withdrawing crypto.
  • Passkeys: MEXC supports passkeys that easily let you verify yourself using your fingerprint, face recognition, or device PIN instead of entering normal verification codes every time.
  • Anti-Phishing Code: You can create your own anti-phishing code, which MEXC then displays inside genuine emails sent to your account. Hence, it helps you identify fake emails.
  • Withdrawal Address Whitelist: You can turn on a withdrawal whitelist so crypto can only be sent to wallet addresses you have already approved. Also, MEXC even offers a security restriction that places a 24-hour waiting period on newly added whitelist addresses.
  • Account Freeze: MEXC lets you freeze your account quickly when you believe someone else has gained access to it.

Asset Protection

MEXC mainly backs user funds with a $100 million Guardian Fund. This one is built specifically to cover users if the platform ever suffers a hack or major technical failure, and MEXC says it also protects user assets through cold and hot wallet separation. Now, on top of that, the futures side runs its own risk reserve fund, which has held more than half a billion dollars in crypto assets.

MEXC also publishes monthly proof-of-reserves reports, and recent figures show reserve ratios staying pretty healthy, well above 100% for major coins. Hence, this means the exchange holds more crypto in reserve than users technically have on deposit.

What Are the Unique Trading Features of MEXC?

The unique trading features of MEXC are crypto spot trading, high-leverage perpetual futures, stock futures integration, automated bots, and copy trading.

Crypto Spot Trading

MEXC spot trading gives you access to one of the largest selections of cryptocurrencies among major centralized exchanges, with over 3,000 coins and a large range of spot pairs. Here, you can buy the actual crypto using pairs such as BTC/USDT or ETH/USDT, and the purchased coins then appear in your Spot wallet.

You can either place a market order when you want to buy or sell quickly, or use a limit order when you want to choose your own price. MEXC also gives you more order controls than just basic market and limit orders. The spot platform supports TP/SL, OCO, and trailing stop orders.

MEXC pairs its spot market with popular tools like grid bots and dollar-cost averaging, so even a beginner can easily automate a basic buy-low strategy without watching charts all day. The web platform is also easy to access from a browser if you prefer a desktop-style layout.

Crypto Perpetual Futures With High Leverage

MEXC’s futures market lets you trade over 900 perpetual contracts, with leverage reaching up to 200x on BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT pairs. Remember, altcoins have generally lower maximum leverage compared to BTC or ETH.

Currently, the exchange offers USDT-M, USDC-M, and Coin-M futures. USDT-M futures are the easiest to understand because you use USDT as both your margin and settlement currency.

Now, for USDC-M, you will be using USDC as a settlement currency, and for Coin-M, you will be using an underlying currency like BTC or ETH as a settlement currency. MEXC also supports cross margin and isolated margin, along with limit, market, trigger, and other advanced order types.

Stock Futures Integration

MEXC Stock Futures let you trade the price movement of major U.S. stocks directly from its futures platform. You can use crypto such as USDT as margin.

The trading platform currently offers stock futures linked to companies such as Apple, Nvidia, Tesla, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Coinbase, Robinhood, and McDonald’s, along with other available contracts.

Actually, MEXC uses the same general trading interface as its crypto perpetual futures, so the controls will already look familiar to you if you have used MEXC futures before. You can take both long and short positions, and some stock futures contracts even support leverage of up to 200x.

Automated & Copy Trading

MEXC offers many automated trading tools on desktop/browser access and its mobile apps. The main options include Spot Grid, Futures Grid, AI-assisted Futures Grid, and Futures Copy Trading.

Well, grid trading automatically places buy and sell orders inside a price range that you choose. Here, you need to set the upper price, lower price, number of grids, and investment amount, and the bot then tries to buy lower and sell higher as the market moves between those levels.

MEXC also provides futures grid trading, and you can run up to 10 futures grid bots at the same time. The feature currently works with USDT-M futures. Plus, its AI mode can study historical data to suggest the price range, number of grids, and leverage for you. User reviews often praise MEXC’s intuitive interface and easy navigation, while the app is also noted for stable, fast execution.

MEXC’s copy trading tool lets you automatically mirror the trades of experienced traders. You can compare traders using information such as ROI and PNL and then select the futures pairs you want to copy.

What Are MEXC Supported Cryptocurrencies and Trading Markets?

MEXC supports more than 3,000 digital assets along with many new altcoins and memecoins, and several crypto, futures, fiat, and stock-linked markets.

MEXC Supported Cryptocurrencies

MEXC supports major cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Cardano, Dogecoin, Tron, and Litecoin. Plus, the stablecoins list includes USDT and USDC, while the wider list shows the exchange supports exposure to both mainstream assets and very new micro-cap projects across DeFi, meme coins, AI tokens, GameFi, Layer 1, Layer 2, DePIN, and real-world assets. Spot trading covers over 3,000 pairs, while the futures side runs more than 900 perpetual contracts. Many of these smaller tokens also appear on MEXC before they become widely accessible on decentralized exchanges.

MEXC Supported Trading Markets

MEXC’s supported markets span more than 170 countries, making it one of the most widely available crypto exchanges anywhere. Now, a specific set of jurisdictions stays fully blocked, though, and that list currently includes the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Mainland China, Hong Kong, and Singapore, alongside sanctioned states like North Korea, Iran, Cuba, and Sudan, plus several Russian-controlled regions of Ukraine. The European Union sits in a gray zone right now too, since MEXC holds no MiCA license.

How to Open a Trading Account on MEXC Crypto Exchanges

You can open a MEXC account by checking country eligibility, registering with an email or phone number, completing KYC, securing the account, and adding funds.

Step 1. Check your country first: You must not live in or access the exchange from a prohibited region. Plus, using a VPN to hide a blocked location breaks the “User Agreement” and can put withdrawals at risk.

Step 2. Open the official website or app: Visit the MEXC Global ltd official website, enter your email address or phone number, and create a unique password. Add the referral code as well. So, enter “mexc-bestbonus” in the referral field to link the fee discount and eligible new-user tasks. MEXC sends a one-time code to your email or phone. Enter it to finish the basic registration.

Step 3. Complete identity verification: Now, go to the “Identification” section in your account security tab. Select your country and document type, upload a clear ID, and finish the face check if the chosen level asks for it. You must also add security settings like 2FA, phishing codes, etc.

Step 4. Deposit or buy a small amount first: Go to the “Deposit” button under “Assets”, choose the exact coin and network on both platforms. We would suggest using a test transfer before moving a large balance. If supported, you can also deposit fiat currency under the “Buy Crypto” section.

Step 5. Place the first trade: Finally, you can visit the “Trade” section. Spot is the simpler starting point, and futures should wait until you understand margin, funding, liquidation price, and stop-loss orders.

Does MEXC Require KYC?

MEXC may or may not require KYC for trading, depending on your region. You see, MEXC used to be a no-KYC exchange, but nowadays, due to continuous regulatory scrutiny across regions, it has mandatory KYC verification in some countries (we were unable to get the exact list of countries). So, you may expect a KYC message if you are in highly regulated crypto countries.

Now, without KYC verification (wherever supported), MEXC has daily withdrawal limits of 10 BTC every 24 hours. You can increase your limit by completing either Primary or Advanced KYC, as higher limits generally require identity verification and may vary by region. Primary KYC allows withdrawals of up to 80 BTC within 24 hours, while Advanced KYC increases this limit to 200 BTC and includes additional features like OTC trading.

What Documents Are Required for KYC?

MEXC’s Primary KYC tier asks for a government-issued ID, like a passport, national ID card, or driver’s license.

Advanced KYC adds a proof of address requirement on top of that, usually a recent utility bill, bank statement, or official government letter dated within the last three months. Plus a live selfie to match your face against the document.

Also, institutional accounts need company registration paperwork and board-level documentation instead of personal ID. Every photo needs to be clear and unedited, since blurry or altered images are a common reason verification gets delayed or rejected.

How Long Does MEXC Verification Take?

MEXC verification normally finishes within about 15 minutes, but a review can take 8 to 24 hours. Actually, a busy market period, blurry image, data mismatch, unsupported document, or failed face scan can even make it slower.

Can You Withdraw Money From MEXC?

Yes, you can withdraw money from MEXC, though the process works a bit differently than a typical bank-linked exchange. If a withdrawal issue comes up, MEXC offers 24/7 customer support through live chat and email. You see, MEXC does not support direct fiat withdrawals to a bank account in most regions, so you need to either use the built-in P2P marketplace or move your crypto to a second exchange that does support bank withdrawals.

Now, through P2P, you must sell your crypto directly to another user who pays you through bank transfer, and MEXC holds the funds in escrow until both sides confirm the trade went through. The alternative route sends your crypto, usually a stablecoin like USDT, to an exchange such as Binance, Kraken, or Coinbase, where you sell it and then withdraw the cash straight to your bank. Some users also report delayed withdrawals, especially when compliance checks or P2P disputes are involved. Fiat support remains limited, and the exchange supports cash-out mainly through P2P or transfers to another platform rather than direct bank rails in most regions.

What Are the Alternatives to MEXC?

The best MEXC alternatives are Binance, Bybit, Coinbase, and Kraken. Here is a quick comparison:

Kraken350+0.40% / 0.80% at the starting tierYes, up to 50x in eligible non-US marketsYes, with 100+ licenses and registrations across 30+ countriesUS, UK, and Canada

Who Should Use MEXC?

You should use MEXC if you want access to a large altcoin selection, low trading fees, high-leverage futures, copy trading, built-in trading bots, and other unique features.

  • Altcoin traders: MEXC is really a good fit for you if you mainly look for early access to smaller or newer cryptocurrencies. As discussed earlier, the exchange lists thousands of spot trading pairs, so you get more choice than on many larger regulated platforms.
  • Futures traders: You can prefer MEXC if you actively trade perpetual futures and want access to high leverage. Well, some selected BTC and ETH contracts can offer leverage of up to 200x.
  • Active traders looking for low fees: MEXC can work well if you trade frequently and want to keep trading costs very low. Its standard spot and futures fees are very low compared to other exchanges like Binance or Bitget, and some spot campaigns offer zero fees on eligible pairs.
  • Traders who use bots or copy trading: MEXC is useful if you want to automate part of your trading instead of placing every order yourself. You can use grid bots, AI-assisted futures grid tools, and copy trading from the same account.
  • Professional traders who want more market choices: MEXC suits experienced traders who want access to spot, futures, stock futures, and advanced order types in one place, and it can also appeal if you want extras like a token issuance platform and occasional token sales alongside the main exchange. Basically, you get a lot of advanced tools, but the platform can feel a bit much for someone completely new to crypto.

Now, who should avoid MEXC? Mainly, beginners who want strong consumer protections, direct bank withdrawals, and a fully regulated home base in the US or UK, though, should probably look elsewhere, since MEXC simply is not built for that kind of user; beginners looking for demo accounts that mirror live markets may also prefer a more education-first setup.

title: U.S. Targets $1.2 Billion From Binance Hack—Where Is the Rest?
summary: U.S. authorities have court authority over more than $1.2 billion from the Binance hack. Binance says it has replaced affected assets, while the hunt for stolen coins continues.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BNB ETH

U.S. authorities have court authority over more than $1.2 billion from the Binance hack. Binance says it has replaced affected assets, while the hunt for stolen coins continues.

The Binance hack recovery has reached a significant milestone: U.S. authorities say more than $1.2 billion in stolen cryptocurrency is subject to court-authorized seizure or restraint. But that headline leaves a much larger question unanswered: what happens to the rest?

The Justice Department’s November 12 announcement puts the broader frozen total above $2.7 billion following the October theft. Crucially, the $1.2 billion is included in that figure. Adding the two would exaggerate the recovery, while calling either sum customer repayments would go further than the announcement supports.

Separately, Binance says it has completed coverage of the affected assets, having committed more than $6.34 billion in company funds to source replacement tokens through market and over-the-counter purchases. Its update says withdrawals continue reopening in phases.

That is a distinct milestone: replacing assets from company resources restores backing without recovering the original coins from the attackers. The law-enforcement totals should therefore not be read as a measure of how much Binance has replaced for customers.

Binance hack recovery: three numbers, three meanings

The FBI attributes the attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor actors and dates the theft to around October 29. Its alert values the stolen assets at more than $6 billion.

That is the starting point. The frozen total describes assets intercepted by government and private-sector efforts. The court-authorized figure identifies a portion covered by seizure or restraint authority. Those are stages of intervention, rather than three separate piles of money.

“We worked together to freeze this massive criminal fraud in its tracks,” U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro said in the DOJ statement.

The language matters because a successful interception is not the end of a recovery. Establishing control, resolving legal claims and determining how assets can be returned are different questions. The announcement gives no timetable for completing that process.

The trail runs through Ether and crypto’s trading infrastructure

The FBI’s October 31 alert said investigators had observed stolen assets being converted primarily into Ether. It warned of further laundering through decentralised finance and instant-swap services and published addresses associated with the operation.

Its appeal extended beyond large exchanges to THORNode operators, RPC providers, DeFi services and blockchain analytics firms. That breadth illustrates the problem: stopping a theft’s proceeds requires action across the routes used to move and exchange them.

Public ledgers can preserve a transaction trail without guaranteeing that every destination can freeze assets. Investigators need both visibility and a point where someone can act. A traceable transfer and a recoverable balance are not the same thing.

For readers following the numbers, a precise remaining-loss estimate would be premature. These are dollar valuations of crypto assets, and the authorities describe lower bounds. Without matching valuation times and complete balances, subtracting one headline from another produces an impression of precision the disclosures do not provide.

A separate operation exposes the human weakness

The same enforcement announcement addressed FaceStealer, a separate North Korean social-engineering campaign. The FBI’s dedicated account of the scheme describes attackers hijacking communication accounts, recording victims’ webcams and using convincing imposter video meetings to compromise new targets.

According to the bureau, that campaign caused more than $400 million in theft over 18 months. Investigators seized over 900 victims’ webcam recordings. Those figures belong to FaceStealer and should not be added to the Binance recovery figures as though they describe one incident.

The disturbing element is the use of familiarity. A message can arrive through a compromised account belonging to someone the target knows. Recorded footage can then make an imposter meeting look like a conversation with a trusted contact.

The FBI also warns that open-source developers and maintainers are being targeted. Access to a developer’s software repository can put downstream users at risk, extending the consequences beyond whatever cryptocurrency is on the initial victim’s device.

Why a blockchain audit is only part of the defence

The implication is uncomfortable for technically sophisticated users: recognising a face, a familiar username or a plausible work request is insufficient authentication. Verification needs a separate route that the suspicious conversation does not control.

A request to install software or change a device during an unexpected meeting deserves particular scrutiny. For teams, the useful question is whether one compromised employee account can reach both operational systems and valuable assets. Separating those permissions can limit the damage.

This is a different threat from a flaw in Bitcoin’s underlying software. BNC’s Bitcoin Core security disclosure coverage explains why identifying the affected layer matters. A sound protocol does not protect a user who grants an attacker access to a device or signing process.

What would make the next update meaningful?

The most useful follow-up would distinguish newly frozen assets from previously announced balances, identify progress toward final recovery and explain whether funds have actually been returned. A larger number alone may conceal very different legal and operational outcomes.

The Binance case shows both sides of crypto’s transparency: stolen funds can remain visible as they move, yet visibility does not automatically stop them. The recovery effort has established a substantial foothold. The unanswered story is how much of that foothold can become a completed recovery—and how much remains beyond reach.

For exchanges, the practical test is readiness before the next incident: knowing who can authorise a response, preserving records and maintaining contact with the services that might receive stolen assets. A recovery operation becomes harder when those relationships must be assembled after funds have started moving.

title: XRP Ledger AI Services Exceed 5,400 Across More Than 190 Merchants
summary: AI agents can now purchase more than 5,400 services on the XRP Ledger, according to t54. Its expanding directory connects automated buyers with providers accepting XRP and Ripple’s dollar-backed RLUSD stablecoin for computing, data, and other digital services. XRPL AI Hub Lists More Than 5,400 Servi...
content:
AI agents can now purchase more than 5,400 services on the XRP Ledger, according to t54. Its expanding directory connects automated buyers with providers accepting XRP and Ripple’s dollar-backed RLUSD stablecoin for computing, data, and other digital services.

Key Takeaways

  • XRPL AI Hub listed 193 merchants offering 5,410 live services.
  • Settled payments topped 15.6 million, with tracked value above $78,000.
  • Monid brought more than 2,600 service endpoints from over 80 providers.

XRPL AI Hub Lists More Than 5,400 Services

Payment infrastructure developer t54 shared on X on Nov. 13 that AI agents, software that carries out tasks on a user’s behalf, could purchase more than 5,400 live services on the XRP Ledger (XRPL). The company stated:

“More services mean more reasons to pay in XRP and RLUSD.”

Dashboard figures checked Nov. 13 put the XRPL AI Hub’s registered merchants at 193, with 5,410 live services and 15,692,399 settled payments. The platform separately showed more than $78,000 in cumulative settled value. Its directory counts individual offerings, allowing one merchant to provide multiple services.

How Agent Payments Grew From 1 Million to Nearly 12 Million

July marked the hub’s launch as agent payments approached 1 million. J. Ayo Akinyele, head of engineering at RippleX, Ripple’s blockchain development arm, discussed the 1 million transaction milestone on July 21. His comments described the early development of tools and standards for autonomous spending on XRP Ledger.

By Oct. 3, tracked activity had reached nearly 12 million x402 payments, extending that earlier milestone. Akinyele identified data purchases and AI model use as leading applications. Available offerings also covered financial data, risk, and credit, broadening the resources automated buyers could access.

How Agents Purchase Services With XRP and RLUSD

Under x402, a payment standard for web requests, a provider returns its price and payment requirements before supplying a service. The buyer signs a transaction, and t54’s facilitator acts as a payment intermediary. It verifies that transaction against the requirements, submits it to XRPL, and returns the settlement result while the payer retains control of private keys.

Ripple’s XRPL AI Starter Kit is a collection of developer tools and integrations that includes x402 support contributed by t54. Agents can purchase API access, computing, and AI inference—the use of trained models to generate answers or other outputs—with XRP or RLUSD. Its wallet tools support balance checks, payments, and transaction tracking.

Providers set their own prices, with RLUSD supporting dollar-denominated payments alongside XRP purchases. Examples listed on the hub include AI model access at 0.0005 RLUSD per request and cryptocurrency token analysis at 0.001 XRP per request.

Beyond XRPL, the broader x402 standards effort supports multiple payment methods for automated commerce. Ripple joined the Linux Foundation-backed group as a premier member in July. Other participants include Visa, Stripe, Google, and Mastercard, connecting payment companies with technology providers.

Large catalogs from individual merchants contribute to the hub’s service count. Monid Tool Router, which brings together services from multiple providers, joined the hub Oct. 20 with more than 2,600 pay-per-call offerings drawn from over 80 providers. Those services were priced in RLUSD.

title: Grayscale Sees New Crypto Opportunities as Bitcoin’s Grip Weakens
summary: Grayscale said crypto’s expansion is creating investment opportunities beyond bitcoin as sectors differ in business models, adoption, and token economics. The firm’s latest analysis linked declining correlations with a stronger role for individual asset selection, while acknowledging persistent mark...
content:
Grayscale said crypto’s expansion is creating investment opportunities beyond bitcoin as sectors differ in business models, adoption, and token economics. The firm’s latest analysis linked declining correlations with a stronger role for individual asset selection, while acknowledging persistent marketwide risks.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin explained about half the variation in crypto sector returns.
  • Among the 10 largest non-stablecoin assets, six led quarterly performance over two years; bitcoin led none.
  • Crypto sectors became less correlated, broadening diversification potential.

Grayscale Finds More Than a Bitcoin Trade

Crypto asset manager Grayscale said on Nov. 12 that differences in business models, adoption, and token economics—the rules governing supply and holder incentives—were widening investment opportunities beyond bitcoin. Zach Pandl, Grayscale’s head of research, and Charlie Perkins, research associate, outlined the findings in their assessment of crypto’s expanding investment opportunities.

The commentary stated:

“As crypto matures, investors have more opportunities to seek differentiated returns through sector and asset selection beyond bitcoin exposure alone.”

Common market forces remain powerful, the authors noted, even as sectors become less correlated.

Over three years, bitcoin explained about half the differences in how much sector returns rose or fell in the firm’s analysis of crypto investment risk. The comparison used the FTSE Grayscale Crypto Sectors, indexes grouping digital assets by function and use case. Among the 10 largest non-stablecoin assets, six different cryptocurrencies led quarterly performance over two years; bitcoin topped none of those quarters. The performance comparison used data through Nov. 4.

Business Models Give Asset Selection More Weight

Grayscale’s earnings-based approach to token valuations examines fees generated by trading, lending, and other applications, alongside operating costs and distributions. Buybacks repurchase tokens, while staking rewards compensate holders who commit assets to support a network or protocol. New issuance creates tokens, and unlocks release previously restricted holdings; both can increase circulating supply and offset those benefits.

Tokenized equities provide another example of how adoption can affect networks differently. In July, Grayscale identified Ethereum, Solana, BNB Chain, Avalanche, and Canton Network, a public blockchain built for regulated markets, as potential beneficiaries of equity tokenization. Its analysis distinguished third-party wrappers, tokens representing claims on shares held through a separate entity, from issuer-sponsored shares issued directly on a blockchain. These models and regulated securities infrastructure could favor different networks.

That focus extends Grayscale’s broader argument about crypto’s role alongside concentrated stock holdings. In September, Pandl argued that digital assets could diversify crowded equity exposure without replacing stocks as a core holding. The latest findings address a separate question: how exposures differ within crypto itself.

Lower Volatility Still Leaves Portfolio Risks

Bitcoin’s annualized realized volatility, a measure of historical price fluctuations, was in the mid-40% range as of Oct. 31, down from triple-digit levels in earlier cycles, according to Grayscale. Extreme moves and momentum remain defining characteristics, with gains clustering and reversals turning sharp. Lower historical volatility therefore coexists with substantial price risk.

Schwab’s analysis of crypto portfolio allocations offers a complementary qualification: even small bitcoin or ether positions can significantly affect overall performance. Its framework considers expected returns, volatility, and correlations, or alternatively a risk budget, the share of overall portfolio volatility allocated to a holding. Different price behavior across tokens does not ensure protection during declines.

Within crypto, diversification and position sizing address different aspects of exposure: the spread across holdings and the capital committed to each. Grayscale’s historical portfolio tests reflected bitcoin’s strong realized performance during the study period and should not be treated solely as forecasts.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, OpenAI launched AI payments in ChatGPT, Jane Street nearly eightfold its Fidelity Bitcoin ETF holdings while trimming its BlackRock stake, and Trump nominated four SEC and CFTC commissioners, including a replacement for Hester Peirce.

OpenAI launches AI payments in ChatGPT with Visa, Mastercard and Amex

OpenAI on Friday introduced a new feature allowing AI agents to make purchases on behalf of users directly within ChatGPT through existing payment networks, in collaboration with American Express, Mastercard and Visa.

The wallet lets users authorize transactions using biometric verification, such as facial recognition or fingerprints. Payment networks generate tokenized card credentials for each approved purchase, keeping users’ actual card details from merchants and AI agents, the company said.

The service is being rolled out to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US with eligible cards issued in the country. OpenAI said it plans to eventually support purchases within preset spending limits and other restrictions without requiring approval for each transaction.

The launch comes as AI companies seek to move beyond product recommendations into executing transactions, potentially changing how consumers interact with online merchants. OpenAI said it is working with payment processors and fraud prevention firms to support AI purchases through existing checkout systems.

Jane Street boosts Fidelity Bitcoin ETF holdings nearly 8x, trims IBIT

Jane Street’s share count in Fidelity’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) rose nearly eightfold in the third quarter, while its holdings in BlackRock’s fund fell 19%.

The trading giant ended September with 7.01 million shares of Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC0, up from about 887,000 at the end of June. The position was worth $509 million on Sept. 30, according to its second-quarter and third-quarter filings.

Jane Street’s holdings in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) fell to 20.22 million shares from 24.88 million. A higher share price lifted the reported value of its stake to $957 million from $828 million.

Jane Street was the largest reported institutional holder of BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF at the end of June after boosting its share count by 324% in Q2, according to 13F Pro. IBIT is the world’s largest spot Bitcoin ETF with $56 billion in net assets as of Thursday.

The firm also added nearly 9 million shares (about $249 million) of the ARK 21Shares Bitcoin ETF (ARKB), while more than doubling its holdings in BlackRock’s iShares Ethereum Trust ETF (ETHA) by 7.83 million shares (about $158 million).

Trump nominates Hester Peirce successor among SEC, CFTC picks

US President Donald Trump has nominated Steven Levine to replace former Securities and Exchange Commission Commissioner Hester Peirce, one of the agency’s most prominent crypto advocates, as part of four nominations to fill vacancies at the SEC and Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

The White House’s latest announcement on Thursday named two nominees each for the SEC and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, agencies whose decisions help shape US cryptocurrency regulation, among other functions. All four nominations require Senate confirmation.

The nominations would replenish several commissioner roles. The SEC currently has only two of its five commissioner seats filled, while CFTC Chairman Michael Selig is the sole member of his agency’s five-seat commission.

The nominations come weeks before Democrats are set to take control of the Senate in January, giving a narrow window for Republicans to confirm Trump’s picks.

OpenAI’s new payment wallet lets AI agents complete purchases using existing card networks, with plans to eventually allow preauthorized transactions.

OpenAI on Friday introduced a new feature allowing AI agents to make purchases on behalf of users directly within ChatGPT through existing payment networks, in collaboration with American Express, Mastercard and Visa.

The wallet lets users authorize transactions using biometric verification, such as facial recognition or fingerprints. Payment networks generate tokenized card credentials for each approved purchase, keeping users’ actual card details from merchants and AI agents, the company said.

The service is being rolled out to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US with eligible cards issued in the country. OpenAI said it plans to eventually support purchases within preset spending limits and other restrictions without requiring approval for each transaction.

The launch comes as AI companies seek to move beyond product recommendations into executing transactions, potentially changing how consumers interact with online merchants. OpenAI said it is working with payment processors and fraud prevention firms to support AI purchases through existing checkout systems.

OpenAI joins a growing field of companies developing payment systems for AI agents. Google introduced its Agent Payments Protocol in 2025, while Visa and Mastercard have launched initiatives to support AI-initiated transactions.

Crypto companies are also developing payment infrastructure for AI agents. Coinbase introduced its x402 protocol in 2025, enabling autonomous stablecoin payments for digital services, while Circle launched its Agent Stack in May, allowing agents to hold and spend USDC within predefined limits. Crossmint, which provides stablecoin infrastructure, has taken a different approach, combining stablecoin wallets with traditional card networks.

Global agentic commerce transaction value is expected to reach $1.5 trillion by 2030, according to an April report from Juniper Research, up from an estimated $8 billion in 2026.

title: Adam Back makes case for simpler security as Blockstream launches Bitcoin custody system
summary: Blockstream’s new custody system, developed with Thales, uses dedicated hardware for transaction signing as Adam Back advocates for offline security to reduce cyber risks.
content:
Adam Back’s Bitcoin infrastructure company Blockstream has launched a new institutional digital asset custody solution developed with French technology group Thales, as the cryptographer pushes for simpler, offline security systems to protect Bitcoin against increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks.

The solution, announced Friday, combines Thales’ hardware security modules (HSMs) with Blockstream’s Secure Multi-Party Computation (Secure-MPC) technology, allowing institutions to authorize transactions while keeping sensitive cryptographic operations within dedicated security hardware, according to the company.

Unlike conventional MPC implementations that may perform portions of the signing process outside dedicated security hardware, Blockstream said its architecture executes the entire signing protocol within the protected environment of Thales’ HSMs.

Blockstream co-founder and CEO Adam Back, a pioneering cryptographer whose Hashcash system helped lay the groundwork for Bitcoin’s proof-of-work mechanism, told Cointelegraph that conventional MPC protocols are often too complex and require too much communication between devices to be practical for fully offline cold storage.

“When people talk about MPC, they’re talking about some very esoteric and complicated protocols that are hard to secure and are very interactive. So you can’t really use them in a cold storage setting,” Back said.

Related: Blockstream rejects ransom as Liquid hackers hold nearly 600 BTC

Adam Back makes the case for simpler Bitcoin custody

Back pointed to the Binance $6.3 billion hack as an example of the risks facing internet-connected custody infrastructure, arguing that keeping signing devices offline can help prevent unauthorized access.

According to Binance’s investigation, attackers compromised employee devices and obtained credentials that allowed them to access the exchange’s wallet-signing infrastructure.

If you connect equipment to the internet, even if it’s via firewalls and so on, there is risk that you can get unauthorized access. You can get hackers into the network, get hackers with access to logins they shouldn’t have and so on.

He also said that AI could make existing security challenges more difficult to manage, particularly by helping attackers discover subtle flaws in complex MPC implementations.

“The AIs can help attackers find small implementation errors and things like that, which may not be obvious,” he said.

Asked whether the broader custody industry would adopt similar offline security models, Back said he hoped so, arguing that institutions should “adapt to the environment” by moving assets into cold storage to reduce exposure to potential AI-assisted attacks.

“Complexity is the enemy of security. And going back to basics is the answer, you know, just cold-store it,” Back added.

title: Twenty One Capital’s Bitcoin Gains Fuel First Profitable Quarter at $1.09B
summary: Tether-backed Twenty One Capital reported $1.087 billion in third-quarter net income, largely driven by unrealized gains on its bitcoin holdings.   Twenty One Capital Shares Slide Despite Billion-Dollar Profit Twenty One Capital reported net income of $1.087 billion for the third quarter ended Sept....
content:
Tether-backed Twenty One Capital reported $1.087 billion in third-quarter net income, largely driven by unrealized gains on its bitcoin holdings.

Key Takeaways

  • Twenty One Capital posted $1.087 billion in Q3 profit, largely from unrealized bitcoin gains.
  • Twenty One Capital shares fell on the day despite strong earnings, while operating cash flow remained negative.
  • Twenty One Capital may pursue share buybacks as it seeks new revenue streams and manages $486.5 million in debt.

Twenty One Capital Shares Slide Despite Billion-Dollar Profit

Twenty One Capital reported net income of $1.087 billion for the third quarter ended Sept. 30, a swing of more than $1 billion into profitability largely attributed to a noncash fair-value gain on the company’s corporate bitcoin treasury. However, the release of the third-quarter results failed to reverse a steady decline in the company’s share price over the preceding week.

According to market data, the Tether-backed company‘s stock declined 1%, or 5 cents per share, on Friday, Nov. 13. That pushed the firm’s weekly decline to 9.7%, with a 22% slide over the past month.

The headline profit marked Twenty One Capital’s first profitable quarter since its public debut through a business combination in 2025. In the third quarter of 2025, the company recorded a net loss of $656,000, illustrating how closely its financial results under generally accepted accounting principles track cryptocurrency market valuations.

Bitcoin’s valuation climbed sharply in Q3, rising from about $58,600 at the end of the prior quarter to roughly $83,700 by Sept. 30, 2026. Yet after a lackluster October, the rally unraveled, erasing the bulk of those Q3 gains and pushing the price below $69,000 by Nov. 13.

CEO Rapha Zagury used the accompanying shareholder letter to temper expectations, reminding investors that increases in the value of existing holdings are distinct from operating cash flow.

“We welcome bitcoin’s appreciation. But gains from an asset we own are not the same as earnings from businesses we operate,” Zagury wrote in the letter.

Negative Operating Cash Flow Highlights Profitability Challenges

During the third quarter, the company reported negative operating cash flow, using approximately $1.7 million in operations and bringing its year-to-date operating cash outflow to $13.3 million.

Management emphasized that its long-term objective is to build high-margin, cash-generating businesses around its bitcoin holdings, including mining, lending, treasury operations, and energy-related initiatives, in an effort to establish sustainable, independent revenue streams.

Twenty One Capital has $486.5 million in outstanding principal on convertible notes carrying a 1% coupon and maturing in 2030. Approximately 16,116 BTC, representing more than a third of the company’s total bitcoin treasury, is pledged as collateral against these debt obligations.

The filing also highlighted ongoing enhancements to the company’s corporate governance framework. David Goldschmidt, formerly head of global capital markets at Skadden, was recently appointed to the board of directors and its audit committee, strengthening the company’s oversight as it expands its operations.

Looking ahead, Twenty One Capital’s management continues to evaluate strategic initiatives and capital allocation measures, including potential share repurchases if its stock trades below the underlying value of its bitcoin holdings.

title: Inside Prediction Markets: Kalshi Eyes $65B Valuation in the Shadow of State Bans
summary:
The prediction-market sector is manoeuvring between an escalating legal war of attrition and commercial euphoria. 
While state courts pushed their enforcement perimeter beyond retail apps and straight into clearing, platforms continued to print record volume with the CFTC playing the surreal dual ro...
content:
2026-11-13T23:14:00.000+02:00

Friday, 13/11/2026 | 21:14 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • State pushback escalated as a Louisiana court ordered 10 operators to halt trading, brokering, and clearing.
  • Nine platforms processed $30.4 billion in weekly notional volume, as Kalshi weighed fresh funding at $65 billion.

The prediction-market sector is manoeuvring between an escalating legal war of attrition and commercial euphoria.

While state courts pushed their enforcement perimeter beyond retail apps and straight into clearing, platforms continued to print record volume with the CFTC playing the surreal dual role of industry protector and internal prosecutor.

Louisiana Extends Restrictions to Brokers and Clearers

On November 12, a Louisiana court ordered ten prediction-market operators to block users in the state, including Kalshi, Polymarket US and Robinhood. The court order goes beyond the apps: the operators may not broker, clear or settle event contracts for anyone in Louisiana.

Meanwhile, new platforms continue entering the market via partnerships. A Canadian sports prediction-market company, Prospect Markets, launched in the US as an introducing broker on Crypto.com’s infrastructure.

A day earlier, Underdog, which runs its own CFTC-registered exchange, agreed to make its contracts available through Plaee, whose clients will be able to offer those contracts under their own brands without registering as an exchange.

Crypto.com and Underdog are both among the operators named in Louisiana’s order.

The CFTC Is Fighting a Two-Front War

The CFTC continue fighting the states in court. On November 12, the agency and the United States sued Arkansas to stop its case against Kalshi. They argue that the contracts fall under federal derivatives law.

The same agency is also scrutinising Kalshi. Politico and Reuters reported that the CFTC had privately warned Kalshi it could face charges over how it notified the agency of new contracts.

Kalshi told CNBC the issue was a procedural error involving a handful of contracts, many of which were not live.

Kalshi Eyes $65B Valuation Leap

DeFi Rate recorded about $30.4 billion in notional volume across nine venues for November 7–12, with Kalshi accounting for roughly 78% of that volume.

At the same time, the platform is discussing new funding at a $65 billion valuation, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters on November 12. That would be $25 billion more than the $40 billion post-money valuation of its Series G two weeks earlier.

Polymarket reported revenue growth and job cuts in the same week. On November 10, it told CNBC that its annualised revenue had passed $1.8 billion, up from more than $1 billion in June. That figure is the company’s own run rate, not full-year revenue.

The next day, it confirmed that it had cut jobs and ended contractor agreements. It said the reorganisation followed leadership changes and also included new hires.

title: Kraken parent Payward gains market share as slower trading weighs on earnings
summary: Payward’s adjusted EBITDA fell 66% year over year to $60 million, even as its share of global spot trading nearly doubled and fee-based services expanded.
content:
Kraken’s parent company Payward nearly doubled its share of global crypto spot trading to 6.5% in September from 3.3% a year earlier, even as weaker trading activity weighed on its earnings.

The market-share gain means Payward captured a larger portion of spot trading relative to competitors, rather than an increase in trading activity across its platforms. The company handled $353 billion in transactions in the third quarter, down 30% from a year earlier, according to financial results released Friday.

The two figures measure different things. The market share tracks its portion of global spot trading across its platforms in September, compared with a year earlier, while Payward’s quarterly transaction volume includes activity across multiple products, including spot, margin, equities, payments and certain derivatives.

Adjusted EBITDA fell to $60 million from the $178.6 million reported a year earlier. Total platform margin fell 12% to $487 million. Payward introduced that measure this quarter to replace adjusted revenue, adding a deduction for staking rewards paid to customers.

Acquisitions expand Payward beyond spot trading

Payward has spent the past two years expanding beyond its core cryptocurrency exchange business through acquisitions in derivatives, proprietary trading, tokenized assets and payments. The strategy aims to diversify revenue beyond transaction fees, which fluctuate with market activity.

Its purchases include futures broker NinjaTrader and proprietary trading firm Breakout in 2025, followed by the acquisition of US-regulated derivatives platform Bitnomial in May 2026. The company also expanded into stablecoin payments with its purchase of Reap in July.

Those businesses contributed to a broader mix of trading and service-based activity in the third quarter. The number of derivatives contracts on which Payward charges a per-contract fee rose 84% to 66 million. Margin from subscriptions, trader evaluations and other paid services rose 59% to $125 million.

Breakout, which charges traders for evaluations that can qualify them for funded trading accounts, was included for the full quarter after joining in September 2025. The July purchase of Reap added a stablecoin payments and card-issuing business. The company did not quantify either acquisition’s contribution to the quarter.

Related: Kraken parent Payward acquires Magic Labs’ wallet business

Earnings recover from second-quarter lows

Results improved from the second quarter despite remaining below year-earlier levels. Total transaction volume rose 22%, while total platform margin increased 12% to $487 million from $436 million.

The improvement was not driven by trading alone. Margin earned from assets customers hold on Payward’s platforms, including staking-related services, rose 26% to $128 million. That accounted for roughly half of the $51 million quarterly increase in total platform margin.

Adjusted EBITDA climbed to $60 million from $23 million, while its margin relative to total platform margin rose to 12% from 5%. Compared with a year earlier, however, adjusted EBITDA was down 66%, underscoring the pressure on profitability despite a growing contribution from services less directly tied to trading activity. Asset- and access-based services accounted for 52% of total platform margin, up from 46% a year earlier.

That shift could matter for an eventual public listing. Payward confidentially filed for a US IPO in November 2025 but paused its plans in March as market conditions weakened. By September, the earliest potential listing window under consideration was the second quarter of 2027.

title: US regulators move ahead on crypto trust charters as Senate scrutiny grows
summary: Coinbase’s trust company received final clearance as lawmakers seek records on crypto firms’ compliance and potential conflicts of interest.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 13, 2026

Coinbase’s trust company received final clearance as lawmakers seek records on crypto firms’ compliance and potential conflicts of interest.

Federal regulators are opening more avenues for crypto companies to operate under US rules, while congressional investigators are asking to see the records behind those decisions. Lawmakers want to know how regulators justified new trust charters, how crypto companies handled compliance and what dealings they had with people tied to President Donald Trump’s administration.

On Nov. 9, Coinbase announced that its national trust company had received final approval to open. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted preliminary conditional approval in April. The company said the charter gives its custody business a consistent federal framework.

Lawmakers had been questioning how federal regulators were using their existing authority to expand crypto companies’ reach. In a May 18 letter to the OCC, Sen. Elizabeth Warren challenged at least nine crypto trust-charter approvals, including Coinbase’s earlier conditional approval. She asked for the applications, the legal analyses behind the approvals and any related communications between OCC officials and the White House or Trump family.

Four days before Coinbase’s announcement, Sen. Richard Blumenthal renewed demands for records from Binance, Tether and two Trump-linked ventures. He gave them until Jan. 4, 2027, to turn over the requested records voluntarily and warned that his subcommittee could take other steps to obtain them.

title: DeepSeek’s AI Models Carry Nvidia Blackwell ‘Fingerprints,’ Researcher Says
summary: Will DePue’s analysis claims hidden numerical patterns reveal Blackwell access at DeepSeek and three other Chinese labs, reopening questions about AI chip controls.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: NVDA

Will DePue’s analysis claims hidden numerical patterns reveal Blackwell access at DeepSeek and three other Chinese labs, reopening questions about AI chip controls.

Researcher Will DePue says the numbers inside DeepSeek’s AI models carry a hidden Nvidia Blackwell fingerprint, raising fresh questions about Chinese developers’ access to restricted American computing hardware.

His claim spans six models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group. The unusual evidence trail is the models’ publicly released weights: the enormous collections of numbers that determine how they work.

But the distinction between a striking technical finding and a proven export-control breach matters. The research identifies patterns left when models were initialised. It cannot, by itself, establish where the hardware was located or how access was obtained.

DeepSeek Blackwell claim turns model weights into evidence

“This evidence isn’t based on any insider information or leaking,” DePue wrote in his post on X. He says he searched more than six trillion combinations of hardware layout and random seed to find matches in published models.

The premise is that initialisation leaves a numerical trace. Before training adjusts a model’s weights, software must generate their starting values. DePue argues that how a GPU distributes that work can leave a recognisable pattern that survives subsequent training.

In plain language, the claim is that the finished model still contains clues about the machinery that first set it up. That would make releasing weights a form of transparency extending beyond the model’s capabilities to aspects of its production history.

What the hardware tests showed

DePue says a Blackwell B300 reproduced 445 entire preserved rows in DeepSeek-V4-Flash bit for bit, while a Hopper H100 did not. He also reports reproducing Kimi K3’s pattern on a rented GB200. These are his reported tests; BNC has not independently reproduced them.

DePue has also published a verification repository with selected weight rows and scripts for five models, including the older DeepSeek-V3. It lets readers replay these comparisons; releasing code is not the same as an independent replication.

The November 12 Unemployment Labs report associates DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiniMax-M3 with B200/B300-compatible patterns. DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, Kimi K3.1-Pro and Ant Group’s Ling-3.1-flash match GB200/GB300-compatible layouts. The method does not distinguish individual chip models within those groups.

There is an established reason to care about the exact environment in these comparisons. PyTorch’s reproducibility documentation explains that fixed seeds can reproduce random sequences under controlled conditions, while identical seeds do not guarantee identical results across platforms, versions or CPU and GPU execution.

That documentation does not verify DePue’s findings. It helps explain why a convincing reproduction must specify the software, hardware and settings, rather than rely on a matching seed alone. The engineering details are part of the evidence, not incidental background.

The limits are as important as the fingerprint

An unusually configured AMD MI300X can mimic these layouts. The report excludes that alternative for V4-Flash, but not the other five models. Initialisation also need not use the hardware that subsequently trains a model.

The report is explicit that its findings “do not establish where the chips were located, how access was obtained, or whether export controls were violated.” A hardware match therefore cannot be read as a customs record or proof of a shipment into China.

Those qualifications leave room for a consequential result without accepting every broader inference attached to it. Evidence about one stage of model development can be valuable even when the rest of the supply chain remains unknown.

Why the export-control question is live

The political context predates this report. In February, Reuters quoted a senior Trump administration official alleging that DeepSeek had trained a model on Blackwell despite U.S. restrictions. The official did not disclose how the government obtained its information. That earlier allegation is context, not independent confirmation of DePue’s new tests.

The legal framework also reaches beyond a simple map of chip locations. In May 31 guidance, the Bureau of Industry and Security said pre-existing licensing requirements continued to apply to covered advanced-computing items destined for certain China- or Macau-headquartered entities, including entities outside those destinations, unless an applicable exception was available.

That guidance concerns specified transactions and regulated items. Establishing a violation would require evidence about the parties, permissions and circumstances involved. A technical paper can raise questions for investigators without answering every legal element itself.

Running DeepSeek on Blackwell is a different question

Nvidia’s own technical documentation already describes serving DeepSeek-V4 on Blackwell and Hopper systems. That is inference: running a released model to produce answers. DePue’s analysis concerns the hardware used to generate starting weights, with possible implications for training.

Confusing those stages would make ordinary deployment documentation look like evidence of the disputed development process. It is not. An open model can run on hardware different from the equipment that originally created it.

For investors, the broader issue is how hardware access shapes AI competition and the economics of supplying computing capacity. BNC’s CoreWeave earnings analysis examined the financing burden behind that infrastructure buildout. This report adds a different question: how much outsiders can learn about computing access from the models themselves.

The next useful evidence would be independent reproductions, scrutiny of alternative explanations and responses addressing the findings from the companies named. For now, DePue has supplied a detailed, testable claim. The intrigue lies in what the numbers might reveal—and in the gap between identifying a machine’s trace and reconstructing how it came to be used.

title: DOJ, CFTC Sue Arkansas to Block Kalshi Crackdown as Prediction Market Battle Escalates
summary: The U.S. Department of Justice and Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) have filed a federal lawsuit against Arkansas, seeking to prevent the state from shutting down Kalshi’s prediction markets and imposing potentially hundreds of millions of dollars in penalties. The complaint, filed Thursd...
content:
The U.S. Department of Justice and Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) have filed a federal lawsuit against Arkansas, seeking to prevent the state from shutting down Kalshi’s prediction markets and imposing potentially hundreds of millions of dollars in penalties.

Key Takeaways

  • The DOJ and CFTC sued Arkansas to block its crackdown on Kalshi, arguing that federally regulated prediction markets fall under the CFTC’s exclusive jurisdiction.
  • Arkansas accuses Kalshi of illegal gambling and deceptive practices, seeking restitution, unpaid taxes and penalties that federal authorities warn could total hundreds of millions of dollars.
  • The lawsuit expands a nationwide regulatory battle, with the CFTC challenging state enforcement efforts in 11 states amid conflicting court rulings over whether sports prediction contracts constitute gambling or federally regulated derivatives.

The complaint, filed Thursday in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Arkansas, names the state and Attorney General Tim Griffin as defendants. It argues that federal commodities law overrides Arkansas regulations governing event contracts traded on CFTC-registered exchanges. Arkansas is the 11th state targeted by the federal regulator in its expanding campaign to establish jurisdiction over prediction markets.

The legal intervention follows a Nov. 4 lawsuit brought by Griffin against Kalshi, which Arkansas accuses of operating an unlawful gambling business while misleading consumers about the legality and risks of its products.

As previously reported by Bitcoin.com News, Griffin contends that Kalshi’s sports contracts are effectively unlicensed wagers, regardless of how the company classifies them. Arkansas also alleges that the platform permitted participation by customers aged 18 to 20, below the state’s minimum casino gambling age of 21, and failed to adequately disclose risks involving insider trading and market manipulation.

The state is seeking restitution, unpaid taxes and penalties of up to $10,000 per violation, alongside an injunction stopping Kalshi’s allegedly unlawful activities.

In their new 34-page complaint, federal authorities warn that the cumulative penalties could reach hundreds of millions of dollars. The DOJ and CFTC want preliminary and permanent injunctions preventing Arkansas from investigating or enforcing state laws against federally regulated exchanges and related entities over contracts traded on those markets.

CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig defended the agency’s position in Friday’s announcement.

“The CFTC will continue to defend its sole jurisdiction over these federally regulated markets as granted by Congress under the Commodity Exchange Act,” Selig said, adding that the agency would oppose state interference with its regulatory responsibilities.

The federal government maintains that sports-related event contracts qualify as swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act, placing them within the CFTC’s exclusive authority. Arkansas instead argues that contracts tied to sporting outcomes constitute gambling and remain subject to state consumer protections.

CFTC Takes Aim at State Lawsuits

The Arkansas dispute comes amid increasingly conflicting court rulings nationwide. The CFTC and DOJ previously sued Arizona, Connecticut, Illinois, Kentucky, Minnesota, New Mexico, New York, Rhode Island, Wisconsin, and Utah. Federal courts have granted preliminary protections against state enforcement efforts in Arizona, Illinois, and Minnesota, while other rulings have favored state regulators.

Bitcoin.com News reported that the CFTC’s October lawsuit against Utah followed an earlier federal court decision allowing that state’s gambling restrictions to apply to Kalshi’s sports contracts. Conversely, an October ruling in Illinois blocked the enforcement of certain sports wagering licensing requirements against Kalshi and Coinbase.

The battle has also extended beyond individual lawsuits. In April, a coalition of state attorneys general challenged the CFTC’s position that sports-related prediction contracts qualify as federally regulated derivatives, arguing that the agency’s approach threatens longstanding state protections addressing gambling addiction, underage participation, and sports integrity.

The federal government’s latest complaint introduces another potential conflict involving the CFTC’s Nov. 5 interpretation of its impartial-access requirements. That guidance directs federally regulated exchanges to eliminate certain geographic restrictions within 30 days or explain why compliance is infeasible. Federal authorities argue that Arkansas’s enforcement efforts would effectively force Kalshi to restrict residents’ access, contradicting the agency’s requirements.

The case underscores the growing stakes of a jurisdictional dispute that could determine whether prediction markets operate under a unified federal regulatory system or must accommodate individual state gambling restrictions.

The CFTC said it has also filed supporting briefs in four federal appeals courts and one state supreme court as the nationwide legal fight continues.
