title: OneRoyal Veteran Gebran Massabni Joins PrimaCapital as General Manager
summary:
PrimaCapital has named Gebran Massabni as its new General Manager. He is another former OneRoyal executive joining the management team at the retail FX and CFD broker founded by Ali Marwani. 
Massabni comes to PrimaCapital after spending over 17 years at OneRoyal, where he held several senior roles,...
content:
2026-11-13T21:33:10.816+02:00

Friday, 13/11/2026 | 19:33 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Gebran Massabni joins PrimaCapital after more than 17 years at OneRoyal.
  • He reunites with several OneRoyal alumni at PrimaCapital, including founder Ali Marwani.

PrimaCapital has named Gebran Massabni as its new General Manager. He is another former OneRoyal executive joining the management team at the retail FX and CFD broker founded by Ali Marwani.

Massabni comes to PrimaCapital after spending over 17 years at OneRoyal, where he held several senior roles, including Head of Business Development and Chief Operating Officer. In 2023 he was named Head of Global Sales.

Massabni’s new role at PrimaCapital appears in the speaker program for the Forex Traders Expo & Summit Dubai, which takes place later this month. However, PrimaCapital has not shared details about his responsibilities or when he will officially start.

PrimaCapital Builds Team around OneRoyal

Alumni Massabni is joining a company that already has ties to his previous employer. Marwani started PrimaCapital in 2023 after spending ten years at OneRoyal and its predecessor, Royal Financials, which he joined in 2011. Both companies work in the retail trading sector and offer leveraged products like FX and CFDs.

Massabni brings experience from a well-established, multi-licensed broker to a newer company that competes in similar markets, especially in the Middle East.

He is not the only former OneRoyal employee at PrimaCapital. Public records show that Mohammad Jawad Rashid is now Head of Risk at PrimaCapital after previously working as Head of Market Research at OneRoyal.

It is unclear if these hires are part of a planned recruitment strategy.

UAE Activities Run through a Separate Company

According to its website, PrimaCapital’s main operating company is PrimaCapital Limited, which is registered in Saint Lucia under number 2023-00550. The broker provides CFDs through MetaTrader 5.

PrimaCapital’s activities in the UAE are more limited in scope. The company says that all introducing activities in the country are handled only by Prima Global Financials LLC, which holds a Category 5 licence from the UAE Capital Market Authority.

This licence allows for client introductions and promotion, but not full brokerage or execution services in the UAE. This is an important distinction as Massabni steps into his new role as General Manager.

title: OpenAI Rolls Out ChatGPT Wallet With Visa, Mastercard and Amex
summary: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Wallet to let artificial intelligence (AI) agents complete purchases using customers’ existing payment cards. The initial U.S. rollout requires users to approve transactions and keeps their actual card details hidden from agents and merchants. ChatGPT Wallet Connects AI Sho...
content:
OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Wallet to let artificial intelligence (AI) agents complete purchases using customers’ existing payment cards. The initial U.S. rollout requires users to approve transactions and keeps their actual card details hidden from agents and merchants.

Key Takeaways

  • Access starts with U.S. Pro subscribers age 18 and older.
  • Users keep existing card rewards and eligible dispute protections.
  • Merchants may collect recurring payments under terms users approve.

ChatGPT Wallet Connects AI Shopping With Card Payments

OpenAI began rolling out ChatGPT Wallet on Nov. 13, enabling users to have agents complete purchases on their behalf. OpenAI said ChatGPT had 1.2 billion weekly users, many using it to research products and compare options.

The company stated:

“Built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa, ChatGPT Wallet will initially be available through dots⁠ for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the U.S.”

These personal AI agents, called dots, handle tasks on users’ behalf around the clock, running on their own cloud computers and connecting to more than 4,000 apps through plugins. Users can reach a dot through ChatGPT, Slack, or Teams, while Custom Rules let them permit, block, or require approval for specific actions.

Before an agent-initiated purchase, customers review the items, total, and selected card, then approve payment using Face ID or another supported biometric check. A payment network supplies substitute card credentials, called a payment token, to charge the selected account. The substitute includes a card number, security code, and expiration date for checkout, keeping the actual card details hidden from the agent and merchant.

Wallet’s privacy notice says OpenAI collects purchase, contact, and device information, while its provider collects the full card number. OpenAI receives a tokenized credential and limited card details. The company says Wallet information is not sold or shared for targeted advertising.

U.S. Pro Access Comes With Checkout Restrictions

Eligible users must be U.S. Pro subscribers age 18 or older with a U.S. billing address and supported U.S.-issued American Express, Chase, Mastercard, or Visa cards. At launch, Wallet works only in dot conversations, excluding Chat, Work, and standalone Codex threads. Chase cardholders must be the primary account holder.

Approval allows checkout to proceed, while merchant confirmation establishes whether an order was placed. For recurring plans, merchants may retain the credential and collect subsequent payments under the agreed terms. Card issuers handle declined, disputed, or unrecognized charges, while sellers manage cancellations, returns, and refunds. Under its Wallet terms, OpenAI generally does not decide or fund merchant refunds or card chargebacks, except when legally required or separately promised.

Merchant security systems can block agents or decline legitimate purchases, OpenAI said. Its Commerce Partner Playbook addresses product information, website access, and payment compatibility, while businesses retain control over pricing and fulfillment. In Oct. 2025, Cloudflare announced an authentication collaboration with Visa, Mastercard, and American Express, using Web Bot Auth to help websites identify trusted agent traffic.

Payment Networks and Crypto Firms Develop Agent Tools

Mastercard’s broader work includes its Agent Pay framework, which it described as requiring agents to register and undergo verification while consumers control permitted purchases. Its agentic tokens extend technology already used for contactless payments and saved cards.

Visa pursued developer integration through its investment in Replit. The companies said they were working to integrate Visa Intelligent Commerce into the development platform. Their stated goal was to let developers build applications and agents capable of initiating transactions and accepting payments.

Moonpay offered another approach when it launched PayBox in July, connecting to ChatGPT and Claude through a custom connector. Users can require passkey approval for each transaction or authorize actions within preset limits.

Blockchain-based systems also support agent payments under delegated authority, allowing software to hold wallets and pay for services. OpenAI expects to support fuller purchase delegation over time, with users setting spending limits, categories, or time periods. Its planned model would let users pre-approve purchases within those limits.

title: Bitcoin Could Rebound to $90K but Risks $65K Retest: 21shares Strategist
summary: Bitcoin could recover toward $87,000 and eventually exceed $90,000, according to 21shares strategist Matt Mena. He linked the outlook to renewed buying after softer-than-expected producer inflation, while identifying support and resistance levels that would shape the recovery. Strategist Maps Bitcoi...
content:
Bitcoin could recover toward $87,000 and eventually exceed $90,000, according to 21shares strategist Matt Mena. He linked the outlook to renewed buying after softer-than-expected producer inflation, while identifying support and resistance levels that would shape the recovery.

Key Takeaways

  • Mena identified $70,000 and $74,000 as recovery thresholds for bitcoin.
  • Losing support near $69,000 could expose $65,000 to another test.
  • October producer prices rose 0.3%, while annual producer inflation reached 6.5%.

Strategist Maps Bitcoin’s Recovery Toward $90,000

Matt Mena, senior crypto research strategist at crypto investment product issuer 21shares, assessed bitcoin’s rebound in commentary supplied directly to Bitcoin.com News on Nov. 13. The 21shares research strategist described bitcoin as finding support around $69,000 and retesting $70,000 following the producer price index, or PPI, release. The index measures prices received by U.S. producers.

“We view this bounce as an encouraging sign that buyers are stepping in as selling pressure eases, though a sustained recovery will require bitcoin to reclaim $70K and then $74K,” Mena stated. “Bitcoin is showing immense strength, although it may not seem so, setting higher lows that are ~20% above its $57K cycle low.” He further shared:

“Holding $69K would help establish a base for that recovery, while a break below it would leave $65K vulnerable to another test.”

The higher lows Mena described are successive price troughs above earlier ones, measured against the $57,000 cycle low he cited.

PPI Offers Relief as Annual Inflation Accelerates

The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Friday morning that producer prices rose 0.3% in October, slowing from September’s revised 1.4% increase. Annual producer inflation nevertheless accelerated to 6.5% from 6.3%, reaching its highest rate since November 2022. Excluding food, energy, and trade services, prices increased 0.5% monthly and 4.9% annually.

Before the inflation release, bitcoin had rebounded from an intraday low near $67,500 to nearly reclaim $70,000 soon after the report release. That recovery followed a decline through $74,000, $72,000, and $70,000. Trading volume during the rebound remained modest compared with the preceding selling. The price of bitcoin recently sat below $69,000 as the recovery cooled once more.

The rebound also followed a substantial liquidation wave, with crypto liquidations reaching $1.62 billion over a 24-hour period. Bullish positions accounted for $1.46 billion of that total. Forced selling added pressure as leveraged positions were unwound across bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies.

Institutional demand remained under pressure, with U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs recording $284.1 million in net outflows on Nov. 12, their sixth consecutive session of withdrawals. Blackrock’s IBIT accounted for $203.8 million of the total. Those redemptions preceded the PPI release and Mena’s assessment of renewed buying.

August Rally Informs the Longer-Term Outlook

In technical analysis of bitcoin’s price movements, support marks an area where buying could slow a decline; resistance marks an area where selling could impede an advance. From $69,000, reaching $87,000 would require approximately a 26% gain, while $90,000 would represent about a 30% advance.

The strategist had previously outlined a potential move toward $90,000 in commentary supplied Oct. 14, when he identified $85,000 as resistance. His latest outlook retained that possibility after the subsequent sell-off and drew on seasonality, or recurring performance patterns during particular periods of the year.

Explaining that outlook, Mena said: “It is also worth remembering how quickly bitcoin can move once momentum turns. Bitcoin’s late-August surge from roughly $62K to $78K in just three days, a 25% move, shows how quickly upside momentum can return.” He continued:

“A recovery toward $87K and an eventual push above $90K could still be in the cards, especially when seasonality is factored in, as Q4 has historically been the best quarter for bitcoin, averaging over 61% returns.”

“For now, defending support and reclaiming the levels lost this week are the first steps,” the strategist concluded.

title: Metaplanet swings to $170M loss as Bitcoin sale hits earnings
summary: Bitcoin sales, valuation losses and rising borrowing costs weighed on the Japanese company’s earnings despite higher revenue and operating profit.
content:
Metaplanet swung to a $170 million net loss in the first nine months of 2026, hit by a decline in the value of its Bitcoin holdings and a loss on the sale of 10,000 coins to demonstrate its ability to raise cash.

The Japanese company, the world’s second-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin (BTC) holder, posted a net loss of 27.16 billion yen (about $170 million), compared with a profit of 13.53 billion yen ($84.6 million) in the same period last year. A 19.17 billion yen ($119.8 million) loss on the Bitcoin sale and an 8.04 billion yen ($50.3 million) loss from a decline in the value of its Bitcoin holdings outweighed gains in the operating business.

Over the quarter, Metaplanet sold the 10,000 BTC for 124.7 billion yen and temporarily held the proceeds in cash, stablecoins and other liquid assets. It then spent 149.9 billion yen to buy 11,000 BTC, paying 9.3% more per coin on average. The company said the sale was meant to show rating agencies and bond investors that it could turn its Bitcoin into cash to meet financing obligations. At the end of September, holdings rose by a net 1,000 coins to 44,000 BTC.

Top 10 largest Bitcoin treasury companies. Source: BitcoinTreasuries.NET

Metaplanet borrowed against its Bitcoin holdings during the quarter, increasing the amount it owed under the credit line to $649.5 million at the end of September from $414 million at the end of June.

The company said it funded Bitcoin purchases from the second quarter onward with money borrowed under the credit line, proceeds from bond sales and the exercise of stock acquisition rights, and revenue from its Bitcoin options business.

Metaplanet’s interest expense rose 56% from the previous quarter to 1.36 billion yen ($8.5 million). Short-term borrowings and bonds payable totaled 110.5 billion yen ($691 million) at the end of September.

For the nine months through September, revenue rose 30.5% to 5.9 billion yen ($36.9 million), while operating profit increased 26.5% to 3.48 billion yen ($21.8 million). The company cut its full-year revenue forecast to 6.5 billion yen ($40.6 million) from 16 billion yen ($100 million).

Related: Metaplanet to take 93.7% stake in Super League through 2,100 BTC deal 

Bitcoin treasury companies face pressure from falling prices, index removals

Metaplanet’s earnings come as Bitcoin treasury companies face mounting pressure from incoming stock index removals and falling Bitcoin prices.

Index provider MSCI confirmed Wednesday that Strategy, Metaplanet and Upexi would be removed from its equity indexes at the Nov. 30 market close, potentially prompting funds that track those benchmarks to sell the shares. JPMorgan previously estimated that Strategy’s removal could result in roughly $2.8 billion in selling pressure from MSCI-linked funds.

Bitcoin fell below $70,000 on Friday and was trading around $68,600 as of 4:51 p.m. UTC, down about 9% over the previous week, according to CoinGecko data.

title: Coincheck Scraps Aplo Brokerage in $18.8M Reversal, Folding Tech into 3iQ
summary:

The group recorded an $18.8 million impairment tied to Aplo for the quarter ended September, contributing to a $26.3 million net quarterly loss, compared with a $2.3 million profit ...
content:
2026-11-13T19:58:47.139+02:00

Friday, 13/11/2026 | 17:58 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Aplo has closed onboarding and entered a phased withdrawal mode through 27 January.
  • Coincheck is repurposing Aplo architecture to power segregated institutional crypto portfolios (SMAs) under its 3iQ subsidiary.

Coincheck Group is winding down its French institutional crypto prime broker, Aplo, just 13 months after acquisition.

The group recorded an $18.8 million impairment tied to Aplo for the quarter ended September, contributing to a $26.3 million net quarterly loss, compared with a $2.3 million profit a year earlier.

The Tokyo-listed crypto fintech giant abandoned the idea to run a standalone European brokerage. Aplo will end its client services by 12 February 2027, and its intellectual property and trading architecture will become a part of a newly created asset-management subsidiary, 3iQ.

A Three-Month Runway to Unwind Balances

Aplo announced the decision to cease operations on 12 November, immediately closing its doors to new accounts and notifying the institutional clients of the termination of their service agreement.

Under the contractual notice period, Aplo has three months to wind down operations and withdraw funds. All accounts will be switched to “withdraw-only” mode no later than 27 January 2027.

Clients can convert holdings into USDC, EURC, or fiat before sweeping funds to external wallets or bank accounts. Any assets remaining by the February cut-off will be liquidated into euros and wired to clients’ registered bank accounts.

Aplo reported no balance-sheet holes or frozen assets, noting that French regulators are notified of the process. Furthermore, Coincheck highlighted Aplo’s MiCA-compliant status, indicating the closure was driven by commercial viability rather than regulatory rejection.

Technology Harvested for 3iQ’s Managed Accounts

Coincheck acquired Aplo in October 2025, when the brokerage served more than 60 active institutional clients, with plans to expand Aplo’s liquidity access, financing products and execution services for banks and institutional investors.

Thirteen months later, management decided that its technology has greater value inside 3iQ than in a small standalone European brokerage.

Approximately half of Aplo’s current employees have been invited to join 3iQ and work on the separately managed account product.

The project will use Aplo’s software and infrastructure to launch managed crypto accounts (SMAs) for institutions and high-net-worth investors in the first half of 2027.

The ultimate test of the retreat now shifts to execution: whether salvaging Aplo’s code for 3iQ can justify the write-down and recoup value from an acquisition that unravelled in barely a year.

Tether Seeks AI Engineer for QVAC

One of the showcased openings is an AI Inference Engineer QVAC – and this is a remote role located anywhere in the world. The position involves developing and improving the inference engine of the local AI stack developed by QVAC.

The successful applicant will primarily use C++ to ensure efficient implementation of AI models on users’ devices. Raises include deploying models at edge hardware, enhancing inference speed and collaborating with researchers to transition models from Development to Production environments.

Among the specific areas of experience listed by Tether are inference frameworks like llama.cpp and ggml, as well as GPU technologies like CUDA, Vulkan, Metal and OpenCL. Knowledge of large language models, transformers and deep learning is also required.

The role aligns with Tether’s strategy of improving and implementing local AI solutions rather than relying solely on the cloud. The model is aimed at providing options to consumers with more control over their data and at having AI features on their own devices.

AI Tools Are Part of the Job Requirements

While this isn’t an AI engineering role, Tether requires candidates to prototype and showcase product concepts efficiently using AI-coding and design tools.

Experience in product management over at least 8 years, experience of scaling consumer applications, advanced JavaScript and React skills, must be essential. Mobile products and real-time communication services experience needed.

Tether Expands Its Technology Hiring

title: Trump Taps Four SEC and CFTC Nominees in Major U.S. Crypto Regulation Reset Bid
summary:
Key Takeaways: President Trump has appointed four people to three vacant positions at the SEC and CFTC. Among the picks are former CFTC Commissioner Kristin Johnson and SEC man Steven
The post Trump Taps Four SEC and CFTC Nominees in Major U.S. Crypto Regulation Reset Bid appeared first on CryptoNin...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • President Trump has appointed four people to three vacant positions at the SEC and CFTC.
  • Among the picks are former CFTC Commissioner Kristin Johnson and SEC man Steven Levine, in addition to Anonick and CFTC man Matthew Rowland.
  • All four nominations are pending Senate approval now before the nominated persons can enter office.

The White House has proposed filling four senior roles at the two U.S. financial regulators that oversee a big slice of the cryptocurrency market with Senate nominees. The appointments could impact the way digital asset regulations evolve as Washington wrestles with the industry’s regulation.

  • Trump Names Two Nominees for Each Crypto Regulator
  • Four Appointments Could Reshape Regulatory Oversight
    • Senate Confirmation Remains the Next Hurdle

Trump Names Two Nominees for Each Crypto Regulator

The White House announcement dated November 12 identifies two candidates for each agency. Steven Levine (Md.) was nominated for another SEC, to be effective until June 5, 2030. His name appears as the next in line to become the replacement for Hester Maria Peirce whose term is also up.

In Virginia, Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Commissioner Rostin Behnam was replaced by Nathan Anonick, who was nominated for a term to expire on June 19, 2031. Matthew Rowland of Washington, D.C., the fourth nominee, would fill in for the rest of the term that ran through April 13, 2028, held by Summer K. Mersinger.

Read More: SEC Clears Path for Tokenized Stocks With 5-Year Onchain Trading Exemption

Four Appointments Could Reshape Regulatory Oversight

This is because both agencies hold holistic oversight over financial service and financial activities that include working with activities linked to digital assets in the U.S. Nominations are proposed both from different sides. In a report, The Block says that Anonick and Levine are both Republicans, and that Johnson and Rowland are both Democrats.

They also have distinct backgrounds brought to the agencies by means of their job history. Johnson was a former commissioner at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and has commented on digital asset regulation. In its reporting, The Block has mentioned both Anonick and Rowland as being involved in the legislative activities related to cryptocurrencies, such as the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act.

Levine’s nomination is especially significant because he’s nominated to fill the seat of his mentor Peirce, who is one of the SEC’s most prominent voices on crypto policy.

Senate Confirmation Remains the Next Hurdle

The White House announcement doesn’t imply that the four candidates have officially joined either regulator. All nominations must be confirmed by the Senate. The SEC nominees will be heard by the Senate Banking Committee and the CFTC candidates by the Senate Agriculture Committee. Their recommendations then would go to the full Senate for approval.

Adds to a political dimension because of the timing. Republicans could regain control of the Senate in January if the midterm elections show them a narrow victory, Reuters reported.

While awaiting confirmation, the four positions are still vacant. Their eventual appointments could help determine the direction of U.S. oversight for crypto exchanges, digital asset markets and related financial products.

title: Bitcoin Price Today: Negative Funding Rates Signal Growing Bearish Bets as BTC Nears $68K
summary: Bitcoin (BTC) price extended its decline on November 13 as negative funding rates, weakening spot demand, and bearish technical indicators pointed to growing pressure across the market.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Bitcoin (BTC) price extended its decline on November 13 as negative funding rates, weakening spot demand, and bearish technical indicators pointed to growing pressure across the market.

The latest data presents a mixed picture, however, as Hyperliquid whales have returned to net-long positions despite deteriorating futures demand and continued selling pressure. Bitcoin was trading around $68,600–$69,200, leaving the $69,227 support level at the center of its near-term outlook.

Negative Funding Rates Reflect Growing Bearish Sentiment

Bitcoin’s derivatives market is showing signs of increasing bearish positioning as funding rates turned negative across several leading cryptocurrency exchanges. Data shared by CoinGlass on November 13 showed negative BTC funding rates on Binance, OKX, and Bybit, indicating that short positions were paying long traders to maintain their perpetual futures contracts.

Bitcoin funding rates have turned negative across major exchanges, including Binance, OKX, and Bybit, signaling growing bearish sentiment among derivatives traders. Source: CoinGlass/X

Binance recorded a funding rate of -0.0002%, while OKX and Bybit registered -0.0057% and -0.0037%, respectively. Negative funding generally reflects stronger demand for short exposure relative to long positions, although it does not necessarily mean that Bitcoin’s spot market will continue falling.

The shift comes as BTC struggles to maintain its recent recovery. Persistent selling pressure and declining demand have weakened the conditions needed for a sustained rebound, leaving derivatives traders increasingly cautious about the asset’s near-term direction.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Funding rates are particularly useful for understanding market positioning because they reflect the balance between long and short exposure in perpetual futures. When rates remain negative, traders holding short positions pay those maintaining long positions. If the market experiences a sudden recovery, crowded short positions can also create conditions for a short squeeze as traders close their positions.

However, funding rates alone cannot establish the direction of future price movements. Their significance becomes clearer when considered alongside spot demand, trading volume, and broader positioning across exchanges.

Hyperliquid Whales Reverse Bearish Bitcoin Bets After Two Weeks

Despite the negative funding rates, large traders on Hyperliquid have begun shifting their Bitcoin positions back toward the bullish side. Glassnode data shows that Hyperliquid whales recently moved from net-short to net-long exposure after maintaining bearish positions for approximately two weeks.

The chart shows Bitcoin perpetual positions shifting from net-short territory in early November to a sharp recovery into positive net-long positioning. Source: @glassnode/X

The reversal ended their first period of net-short positioning since early 2026. Glassnode’s chart tracks daily mean net perpetual positions, calculated by subtracting short exposure from long exposure. The indicator briefly moved into negative territory in early November before recovering sharply and returning to positive levels.

The positioning change is notable because these traders previously held short positions near a local market top before maintaining long exposure during Bitcoin’s August 2026 rally. Their latest reversal raises questions about whether the group is anticipating another recovery or responding to changing market conditions.

Nevertheless, whale positioning does not guarantee a price reversal. Large traders can adjust exposure for hedging, portfolio management, or short-term trading purposes. Their renewed long bias also contrasts with the broader derivatives data showing negative funding rates across several major exchanges.

This divergence suggests that market participants are not positioning uniformly. While some large Hyperliquid traders have increased their bullish exposure, broader derivatives activity continues to reflect caution.

Bitcoin Demand Weakens as Miner-to-Exchange Flows Surge

On-chain data provides another reason for caution. CryptoQuant reported that Bitcoin’s recent rebound is losing momentum as spot demand weakens and miner-to-exchange transfers increase.

Bitcoin’s rebound is losing momentum as spot demand weakens and miner-to-exchange flows surge, suggesting leverage is unwinding without sustained spot buying support. Source: CryptoQuant/X

The analytics platform described the situation by stating that leverage is unwinding without a sustainable recovery in spot demand. This distinction is important because a reduction in leveraged positions can temporarily stabilize prices without creating the buying pressure needed for a lasting recovery.

CryptoQuant’s data showed a roughly 16-fold increase in miner-to-exchange flows, with approximately 2,077 BTC transferred to exchanges. Such movements can attract attention because miners may send Bitcoin to exchanges before selling or managing their liquidity requirements.

Miner-to-exchange inflows surged 16-fold to 2,077 BTC, while spot demand showed early recovery despite weakening futures demand and persistently negative overall demand. Source: CryptoQuant/X

However, the latest increase requires additional context. A response within the accompanying discussion clarified that nearly the entire transfer was associated with Antpool, which moved approximately 2,077 BTC on November 10. This concentration means the spike should not automatically be interpreted as evidence of widespread miner selling.

Even so, the broader demand picture remains challenging. CryptoQuant’s indicators showed an early recovery in spot demand alongside deteriorating futures demand and persistently negative total demand. This suggests that the recent price rebound has not yet gained consistent support from buyers across the market.

For Bitcoin to establish a stronger recovery, renewed spot accumulation will be important. Without that support, improvements in derivatives positioning could remain temporary.

Bitcoin Price Prediction: BTC Tests Critical $69K Support

Bitcoin’s technical indicators continue to reflect a bearish market structure. TradingView’s technical summary maintained a strong-sell rating, with 16 sell signals, nine neutral readings, and just one buy signal.

The moving-average category was particularly negative, recording 14 sell signals, one neutral reading, and no buy signals. The oscillator group showed a comparatively mixed picture, with two sell signals, eight neutral readings, and one buy signal.

The Short-Term Holder SOPR repeatedly fell below 1 during the correction, indicating that recent Bitcoin buyers were realizing losses as prices declined. Source: CryptoQuant/X

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) stood at 26, placing Bitcoin in oversold territory. Although this reading indicates substantial recent selling pressure, it does not independently confirm that a price bottom has formed.

Other momentum indicators also remained weak. The Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) registered -2,454 and generated a sell signal, while the Momentum indicator stood at -8,185, also indicating downward pressure. Williams Percent Range was the only oscillator among the listed indicators generating a buy signal, at -88.

Bitcoin’s position relative to its moving averages further highlights the weakness. The 10-day exponential moving average (EMA) stood at $73,889, while the 20-day EMA was near $76,036. The 50-day EMA reached $78,156, and the 200-day EMA remained around $76,272.

With BTC trading below these averages, the broader technical structure continues to favor sellers. A recovery would first require the asset to regain nearby resistance levels and establish stronger momentum.

Classic pivot points identify $69,227 as the immediate support level, placing it close to Bitcoin’s latest trading range. The next downside reference is $58,181, corresponding to the S3 pivot. On the upside, the Hull Moving Average near $70,912 represents an initial technical hurdle, followed by the broader moving-average cluster in the $73,000–$80,000 range.

A sustained move below $69,227 could increase downside pressure and bring deeper support levels into focus. Conversely, holding this area and recovering above $70,912 could create room for a short-term rebound.

For now, negative funding rates, weakening spot demand, and bearish moving-average signals continue to weigh on Bitcoin. Hyperliquid whales’ return to net-long positions offers a contrasting signal, but stronger spot buying and a sustained recovery above nearby resistance would be needed to confirm a broader change in market direction.

title: Lithium Market Outlook as $90,650 Spot Meets a Heavy ETF Resistance Wall in Q4
summary: After months of falling prices, lithium prices are beginning to stabilize. On November 12, battery-grade lithium carbonate prices jumped 2.2% to 90,650 yuan per tonne, and futures rose, respectively.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: Li

After months of falling prices, lithium prices are beginning to stabilize. On November 12, battery-grade lithium carbonate prices jumped 2.2% to 90,650 yuan per tonne, and futures rose, respectively.

The Global X Lithium and Battery Tech ETF, on the other hand, dropped 2.64% to $59.46.

This divergence indicates that there is not yet a noticeable improvement in the recovery of lithium-related stocks based on the lithium price on the physical market. The market is currently testing the latest rebound, and if the market can form a sustainable recovery, it will be dependent on technical support and overhead resistance levels.

Lithium carbonate rebounds as futures regain momentum

Lithium carbonate, which is used in battery manufacturing, was sold for battery-grade use in China at 90,650 yuan per tonne, according to Carl Capolingua in his November 12 update on X. The spot benchmark rose by 0.2%, and GFEX futures rose 2.2% to about 90,900 yuan. Prices for spodumene concentrate were $1,170 per tonne for the SMM concentrate index in the meantime. Spot concentrate for Australia was $1,225 per tonne, and lithium hydroxide was 81,550 yuan per tonne.

The price of lithium has gradually begun to stabilize following the selling pressure it has experienced in recent times, the figures suggest. But the overall momentum is not as strong as the daily gains indicate. The prices of battery-grade lithium carbonate decreased 3.2 percent in the week ending Nov. 12, according to SMM. Its average price fell 2,950 yuan from its price level on Friday before rising 200 yuan on Thursday.

The chart that Capolingua shared gives a longer-term perspective of this weakness. Lithium carbonate rose from around 83,100 yuan per tonne at the end of 2025 and began to rally rapidly in early 2026. Source: Capolingua Via X

Finally, it hit 210,580 yuan per tonne in May. But the sellers took the reins following this top and established a price structure in a corrective manner.

The chart identifies several overhead resistance areas, including 172,700–179,440 and 157,200–157,840 yuan. Additional technical reference points are the lower zones at 136,260 yuan and 124,020 yuan. The levels indicate the gradual surrendering of previous price gains in the market. So the continuing decline will require further consolidation before the trend is considered reversed.

Lithium ETF tests support as overhead liquidity builds

In the meantime, the data on TradingView does not reflect the trading of lithium carbonate but rather the trading of the Global X Lithium and Battery Tech ETF. The fund closed at $59.46 on November 12, losing $1.61 or 2.64%. It opened at $59.63, reached an intraday high of $60.05, and touched a low of $59.44. Hence, the closing price was not much higher than the session low, indicating selling pressure.

The daily chart shows a clear bearish structure from the prior trading range. The ETF was trading near $85 in June but has dipped towards $67 in July. Source: TradingView

But this rally was not enough to create lasting upward momentum until buyers took it up to $77 in late August. Selling picked up in September and October, and the ETF has now reached its current price of $59.46.

The liquidity heatmap shows that there is an immediate support area between about $57.50 and $58.50. This area is the closest visible liquidity accumulation to the current price. If the defense is successful, a short-term bottom may be set for the ETF. But if the price drops further below $57.50, it would reveal lower price levels and hinder the recovery process.

Overhead liquidity is concentrated in the $60 to $65 range. Several possible resistance zones are seen extending towards 67-75. The price structure of the ETF looks good on the 62.50 level and above, so it would be good to see this move back towards 65 and above. The push higher from here would give more support to bulls reclaiming control.

Most importantly, these concentration areas of liquidity are not a guarantee of reversals or breakouts. They represent potential markets that can affect price action. Traders should keep an eye out for any potential changes in the ETF’s performance as it nears these levels.

title: Hyperscalers List GPUs at Nearly 2× the GPU-Cloud Price, Fluence Research Finds
summary: The AI Compute Race report prices GPU compute outside the biggest buyers: a three-year commitment cuts the median price by 48%, while 17 of 22 tracked GPU models rose in price over the past year DALLAS, Texas – November 13, 2026 – Fluence has published The AI Compute Race, a report that prices GPU c...
content:
The AI Compute Race report prices GPU compute outside the biggest buyers: a three-year commitment cuts the median price by 48%, while 17 of 22 tracked GPU models rose in price over the past year

DALLAS, Texas – November 13, 2026 – Fluence has published The AI Compute Race, a report that prices GPU cloud compute for every company that is not a frontier lab or a hyperscaler. It was produced with research partners NEAR AI, io.net, Boundless, Phala, Gensyn, Fortytwo, Theta, Compute Labs and GAIB. Its central finding: where a company buys a GPU-hour sets the price. Across H100, H200 and B200 models, hyperscalers list GPUs at 1.98 times the GPU-cloud median, from 1.4 times on the B200 to 2.8 times on the H100. The same H200 lists from $4.08 to $10.60 an hour.

Commitment length matters almost as much as provider choice. Against each provider’s own on-demand rate, a one-year reservation cuts the median price by 21% and a three-year term by 48%. Spot capacity lists at 53% of on-demand, for workloads that can be interrupted.

Buyers who expect GPU prices to fall may need to recheck their budgets. Seventeen of the 22 GPU models tracked by GetDeploying cost more than a year earlier, and the median H100 rents for 13% to 30% more, depending on the window measured.

The report also traces why prices are rapidly rising:

  • Demand moved to open models. Chinese models’ share of OpenRouter tokens among companies in the US, Europe and the Global South rose from 6–13% to 57–67% in under eight months, according to CNBC. Open weights let any company with GPUs serve a near-frontier model on hardware it controls.
  • The biggest buyers locked up the newest supply. The four largest hyperscalers guide $720–740 billion of 2026 capital spending, and the four largest disclosed deals by AI labs and Meta with neoclouds total about $233 billion, three of them “up to” amounts and much of it for capacity not yet delivered.
  • The GPU-hour is becoming a financial asset. CME, ICE and Nodal Exchange have announced GPU futures, each settling on a different price index, while lenders are already lending against GPUs: Lambda’s investment-grade-rated loan priced at 6.78% and Sharon AI’s, with no rating disclosed, at 9.95%.

“Open-weight models are close behind the best closed ones, and companies are switching to them. Any company with GPUs can now serve a near-frontier model on hardware it controls. The GPUs are the hard part,” said Evgeny Ponomarev, Co-founder of Fluence.

The report closes with four ways to pay less for the same compute: compare the same chip across provider types, commit when the workload is steady, match the GPU generation to the model, and look beyond the hyperscalers, since much of the newest neocloud capacity is contracted to labs years ahead.

The full report is available at fluence.ai/compute-race-2026.

About Fluence

Fluence Cloud is a GPU cloud provider with capacity from independent data centers (fluence.ai). Founded in 2017 by Dmitry Kurinskiy, Evgeny Ponomarev and Tom Trowbridge, the company has raised $14 million from investors including 1KX, Multicoin, Distributed Global, Blockchange, Tiger Global and Protocol Labs.

title: Griffin Raises $20M to Bring Stablecoin Payments and Card Issuing to Its Banking Platform
summary:
Key Takeaways: Griffin raised $20 million in a Series B round at a valuation exceeding $100 million. The UK’s bank is set to introduce card issuing, stablecoin reserve and cross-border
The post Griffin Raises $20M to Bring Stablecoin Payments and Card Issuing to Its Banking Platform appeared first o...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Griffin raised $20 million in a Series B round at a valuation exceeding $100 million.
  • The UK’s bank is set to introduce card issuing, stablecoin reserve and cross-border payments via blockchain.
  • It now has over 80 businesses integrated and more than 300,000 customers signed up.

Griffin, a UK-based banking infrastructure provider, announced a Series B funding round of $20 million led by Octagon Partners and valued at over $100 million. The capital will enable the company to move beyond its banking offerings and introduce the ability to support stablecoins and card products to its platform.

  • Griffin Raises $20M to Expand Its Banking Infrastructure
    • Stablecoin Services and Card Issuing Lead New Plans
  • On-Chain Payments Become Part of Griffin’s Expansion
    • More Than 80 Companies Already Use Griffin

Griffin Raises $20M to Expand Its Banking Infrastructure

Other investors in the round were existing investors Notion Capital, A+ Ventures, Nordic Ninja and Breega. Griffin said the investment will support its growth toward profitability while financing the next stage of its product development.

Griffin has grown from testing in 2024 to today’s current platform that has over 80 businesses using it since they became a complete UK bank in 2024. Its customers include Uber, Countingup, Anna Money, Yonder, and Prosper.

Today, it serves over 300,000 underlying retail and business customers and handles almost 10 million payments per year. Unaudited revenues for recurring revenue increased 3.2 times year over year at the end of the financial year Sept. 26, 2026.

With fresh investment, Griffin will be able to add cards and stablecoins to its banking capabilities as the next step, the company’s CEO and co-founder David Jarvis said.

Read More: FSB Pushes Türkiye Toward Dedicated Stablecoin Rules and Tougher Crypto Oversight

Stablecoin Services and Card Issuing Lead New Plans

Two key features are soon launching, and Griffin has invested in them. The first is card-issuing, where Griffin enables businesses to launch corporate and retail-issue debit cards using Griffin’s banking infrastructure.

This would have been the unification of bank accounts, payment services and cards on a single platform. A credit card offering will follow the initial debit card offering, which Griffin also plans to introduce.

The second expansion is on stablecoins. Griffin will build reserve capabilities for business in the stablecoin space and include on-chain payment options for cross-border transactions.

On-Chain Payments Become Part of Griffin’s Expansion

The intended stablecoin services would enable companies to operate on both the blockchain payment system and traditional banking services. Those capabilities are, however, listed as part of Griffin’s Development Road Map, which is not necessarily a reflection of available products for customers.

The expansion would also enable Griffin to enable companies that want to offer both traditional banking products and stablecoins for payments while not constructing the underlying financial framework.

Read More: Visa Adds Monad to Stablecoin Settlement Network

More Than 80 Companies Already Use Griffin

Investors have started to pay attention to Griffin’s growth as demand for embedded banking infrastructure grows. The Octagon Partners emphasized the firm’s regulatory framework with the UK’s Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) and Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), alongside proprietary technology and AI systems.

Paraag Davé, Octagon’s head analyst, also referenced customer growth and revenues since Griffin was granted its banking license, claiming the company was approaching double-digit millions of pounds of revenue per year.

title: FutureBit’s Apollo III Bitcoin Miner Hits Micro Center Shelves in Its First Brick-and-Mortar Launch
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

FutureBit’s Apollo III Bitcoin Miner Hits Micro Center Shelves in Its First Brick-and-Mortar Launch
The Brooklyn company's compact home miner, rated at up to 18 TH/s and starting at $1,099.99, goes on sale Friday at four Micro Center stores, including the chain's new Austin locatio...
content:
FutureBit is putting its Apollo III Full Node on sale Friday at four Micro Center stores, the first time customers can walk into a shop and take home one of the Brooklyn company’s bitcoin miners.

The compact home miner, which also runs a full bitcoin node, will be sold in Brooklyn, Miami, Tustin, California, and Austin, Texas, as those stores open Friday, FutureBit said in a release. The four-store launch coincides with the grand opening of Micro Center’s new Austin store, the chain’s 31st U.S. location and its third in Texas.

Customers will also be able to reserve a unit online for in-store pickup, the company said. It did not say how many units each store has in stock, or what Micro Center is charging for them.

Until now, buyers in North America had to order the machine from FutureBit’s website, where the company says units are in stock and ship in two to three days. Putting it on a computer-store shelf lets a customer look at the hardware, ask how it works and carry it out the same day.

“When we started FutureBit, we made weekly trips to the DIY electronics section at the Brooklyn Micro Center to buy parts,” said John Stefanopoulos, founder of FutureBit. “On Friday, someone can walk into that same store, ask how Bitcoin mining works and take home a miner we designed just down the street. We couldn’t be more excited to work with Micro Center on our first physical store launch.”

A 6-inch miner that also runs a full node

FutureBit’s own shop lists the Apollo III Full Node at $1,099.99 without a storage drive, $1,299.99 with 1 terabyte of SSD storage and $1,399.99 with 2 terabytes. A cheaper, miner-only “Standard” model starts at $899.99 but does not include the full node.

The Full Node is rated at up to 18 terahashes per second in Turbo mode, at about 325 watts. In Eco mode, it is listed at about 12 TH/s and 150 watts, with noise under 35 decibels. A Super Eco mode is listed at about 8 TH/s and 80 watts. Power can be adjusted from 50 to 400 watts, and Turbo mode is much louder, at about 55 decibels. Those power figures are measured at the board and can vary by 10%, the product page says.

The unit is a 6.5-by-6.5-by-6-inch cube that weighs 6.5 pounds, comes with a one-year limited warranty and is assembled in the United States. It uses new 3-nanometer, American-designed chips, a custom controller and 8 GB of memory, and it includes a built-in solo mining pool. Buyers can also point the miner at a standard bitcoin mining pool. FutureBit says the full node and solo-mining features require an SSD, which is not included in the $1,099.99 configuration.

Home mining is not a profit play

Bitcoin Magazine covered the Apollo III’s debut in February, when FutureBit introduced the hardware as a way for individuals to run both a miner and a node at home. The point, the company has long argued, is not to compete with industrial mines on cost.

A single Apollo III at 18 TH/s is a sliver of the bitcoin network. A home-scale setup in that range still faces expected times to a solo block measured in centuries at recent difficulty, Bitcoin Magazine previously noted. Even so, a miner running through FutureBit’s Apollo Solo setup found block 973,262 on Oct. 26 and collected the full 3.154 bitcoin reward.

FutureBit, based in Brooklyn, has built consumer mining hardware since 2015. Stefanopoulos has framed store shelves as a way to put more hash rate and more nodes in living rooms. The company did not say whether the Micro Center test will expand beyond the four stores that began selling the Apollo III on Friday.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Bitcoin holds below $70K as stocks slip despite a cooler US PPI print
summary: Bitcoin was down about 4% on the day amid a tepid market reaction to October’s US PPI reading, which came in below expected levels.
content:
Bitcoin (BTC) hovered around $68,700 following Friday’s Wall Street open, rebounding from an earlier dip to roughly $67,500.

Key points:

  • Bitcoin failed to reclaim the $70,000 mark after hitting about $67,500 on Friday, its lowest level since mid-August.
  • The US Producer Price Index (PPI) rose 6.5% year over year in October, 0.1 percentage points below expectations but still the largest increase since November 2022.
  • Rekt Capital warned that a weekly close below $73,000 could mark Bitcoin’s third break of that support level in 2026.

US PPI sees largest yearly gain since Q4 2022

Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD down 4% on the day after bouncing from a roughly 12-week low near $67,500.

BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

The US Producer Price Index, which tracks changes in the prices domestic producers receive for their goods and services, rose 0.3% month over month and 6.5% year over year in October. Both readings were 0.1 percentage points below market expectations but the annual increase was the largest since November 2022.

“Leading the October advance in final demand prices, the index for final demand goods increased 0.5 percent. Prices for final demand services moved up 0.2 percent,” the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported Friday.

US PPI one-month percentage change. Source: BLS

Stocks showed little sign of relief at the start of the US trading session, with traders still parsing developments around Nvidia after its co-founder and CEO, Jensen Huang, resigned on Thursday.

The S&P 500 was down 1.2% at the time of writing, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index was 1.5% lower.

Nasdaq Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

The PPI release led markets to slightly adjust expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes. Odds of a minimal 25-basis-point hike at the Fed’s December meeting rose from 85.4% on Thursday to 89.7%, while odds of a larger 50-basis-point move decreased from 14.5% to 10.3%, per data from CME Group’s FedWatch Tool.

Fed target-rate probability comparison for the December FOMC meeting. Source: CME Group

Economist Robin Brooks described a 25-basis-point hike in December as “all but inevitable.” He argued, however, against a steeper increase, seeing it as ineffective in the face of current inflation drivers: the oil-price spike from the US-Iran war and potential long-term acceleration in underlying inflation. 

“If high inflation is about the Strait of Hormuz and oil, 75 basis points won’t do anything about that. If the issue is that the pace of underlying inflation has risen, then 75 basis points is much too timid to get this under control,” he wrote.

Related: Stablecoin supply falls $14.2B in biggest 30-day drop since June 2022

Bitcoin eyes repeat of breakdown that preceded $60,000 drop

Crypto trader and analyst Rekt Capital warned that a BTC close below $73,000 on Sunday would mark a support breakdown already seen in 2026.

“Last week’s Weekly Candle Closed below 3 Weekly levels,” he wrote on X, referring to $75,000, $76,800 and $78,300. “This Weekly Candle looks set to do something similar. Which is testament to sell-side momentum still gaining and the bears being in control.”

After each of the two previous breakdowns, Bitcoin fell to around $60,000.

BTC/USD one-week chart. Source: Rekt Capital on X.com

At $68,700, BTC/USD is down 17.7% in the fourth quarter and 11.2% month to date. The quarterly performance is currently Bitcoin’s second worst on record, data from CoinGlass confirms.

BTC/USD quarterly returns. Source: CoinGlass

Solo’s SDK confirms that each JellyJelly account belongs to a real, unique person, after a Solo AI agent passed CAPTCHA on 50+ Discord servers.

San Francisco, United States, November 13th, 2026 – Solo, a privacy-preserving proof-of-humanity company, is bringing its human verification software development kit (SDK) to JellyJelly. The social video app runs on Solana and was co-founded by Venmo co-founder Iqram Magdon-Ismail. The integration lets JellyJelly confirm that every account belongs to a real, unique person, with no government ID and no puzzles to solve.

Magdon-Ismail is co-founder and CEO of JellyJelly and an advisor to Solo. He co-developed the SDK behind the integration, shaping both its architecture and the way new users are onboarded.

The move comes as AI agents learn to pass the tests meant to keep them out. In an experiment run by Solo, an AI agent named Gary joined more than 50 Discord servers overnight and sent over 500 messages. No one identified it as an AI agent.

Gary had two instructions: pass every CAPTCHA challenge and accept the terms of service. It completed both through ordinary browsing and clicking, without any custom exploits.

Solo reads the result as a weakness in CAPTCHA. The challenges test whether a visitor can solve a puzzle, and capable AI agents can solve the same puzzles. Harder tests add friction for legitimate users, but they do little to show that a human is behind an account.

“CAPTCHA was built around the idea that humans could do things bots couldn’t. That’s becoming a harder assumption to make when AI agents can browse, click and solve the same challenges as people,” said Edison Siu, co-founder and CEO of Solo. “Our approach is to verify the human directly. Platforms need to know they’re dealing with a real person. Users shouldn’t have to struggle through more puzzles or upload identity documents to prove it.”

JellyJelly lets users share short videos and send cryptocurrency payments to one another. The rise of AI-generated video and automated accounts has made it harder for social platforms to know who is behind each account. Solo’s SDK brings human verification into that setting. It helps the platform tell genuine users from automated accounts, and it stops one person from registering several verified identities.

The process starts with a facial scan from a standard smartphone camera. Solo converts the scan into a biometric representation and encrypts it on the device using fully homomorphic encryption (FHE). This type of encryption lets a system work on data without ever decrypting it. Solo uses it to compare the encrypted representation against existing records, so the matching step never exposes the underlying data.

Users do not need special hardware or a government-issued ID. Raw facial images are not stored. Apps that use the SDK receive a verification result, not access to anyone’s biometric information.

The same SDK can be added to gaming platforms, payment services and other applications that need to block duplicate accounts or separate real users from automated activity.

Solo is backed by Draper Associates, the venture firm founded by Tim Draper. Draper Associates led a $1 million round in the company in March 2025. Solo was also selected for cohort 5 of the Solana Incubator.

Solo’s human verification technology is already live. The company is now working on tools that would let verified users authorize their own AI agents, so merchants and online platforms can confirm that a real, unique person stands behind each one. Solo also plans to enable AI agents and AI companies to pay verified people for work that only humans can do.

Magdon-Ismail, who co-founded Venmo and helped develop its peer-to-peer payment system, is advising Solo on how people and their AI agents will pay and get paid.

“Venmo made it easy to pay a friend,” said Magdon-Ismail. “The next step is your AI agent paying on your behalf. The business receiving that payment needs to know a real person authorized it. I’m working with Solo to make that process simple for everyone involved.”

About Solo

Solo develops proof-of-humanity technology that lets online platforms check that a user is a real, unique person, without asking who that person is. Its smartphone-based system uses fully homomorphic encryption to compare encrypted biometric data, and partners receive a verification result instead of raw biometric data. Solo provides an SDK for web and mobile applications. The company is backed by Draper Associates and was selected for the Solana Incubator cohort 5. Its first product, SoloMission, lets AI agents collect feedback from verified humans.

title: Robinhood’s Crypto Trading Volume Falls 48% in October as Event Contracts More Than Double
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Robinhood’s Crypto Trading Volume Falls 48% in October as Event Contracts More Than Double
Robinhood customers traded $17 billion of crypto in October, down 48% from a year earlier, while event contracts traded jumped 136% to 5.9 billion.
This post Robinhood’s Crypto Trading Volume...
content:
Crypto trading on Robinhood fell by almost half from a year ago in October, the company said Thursday, as customers traded $17 billion of digital assets while their bets on event contracts more than doubled.

The $17 billion figure was down 21% from September and 48% from October 2025, when crypto notional volume reached $32.5 billion. It covers both the flagship Robinhood app and Bitstamp, the crypto exchange the company bought in 2025.

Volume in the Robinhood app fell to $6.8 billion, down 24% from September and 51% from a year earlier. Bitstamp handled $10.2 billion, down 18% month over month and 45% year over year.

Average daily crypto volume across both platforms came to $548 million, compared with $713 million in September and about $1.05 billion a year ago. Daily average crypto trades slipped to about 700,000 from 900,000 in September and 1.1 million in October 2025.

Event contracts take off as crypto cools

The contrast with Robinhood’s prediction markets business is stark. Customers traded 5.9 billion event contracts in October, up 5% from September and 136% from the 2.5 billion traded a year earlier. Average daily volume reached 190 million contracts.

Robinhood counts crypto and prediction markets on the same 31-day calendar, since both trade every day, so the comparison is apples to apples. Event contracts let users bet on outcomes such as elections, sports and economic data, and October’s tally covered the final weeks before the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

That growth has drawn scrutiny in Washington. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, who is set to chair the Senate Banking Committee in January, plans to crack down on prediction markets and election betting platforms.

The rest of Robinhood’s brokerage held up better than crypto. Equity notional volume rose 2% from a year earlier to $325 billion, and options contracts traded climbed 8% to 289 million. Margin balances reached $22.9 billion, up 39% year over year.

Funded customers rose by about 130,000 in the month to 28.9 million, and net deposits came to $15.1 billion. Total platform assets slipped 3% from September to $383 billion but were up 12% from a year earlier.

Robinhood did not say why crypto activity fell. The release, like all of the company’s monthly updates, is unaudited and preliminary.

Retail pulls back as bitcoin slides

The slump in Robinhood’s crypto numbers lines up with a broader retreat by retail traders. Bitcoin ended September near $83,500 and has slid since, falling below $70,000 early Friday for the first time since August as a hot inflation report raised bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike in December.

Institutional demand has cooled alongside it. U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds posted a sixth straight day of net outflows on Thursday, and BlackRock’s IBIT, the largest of them, bled about $2 billion over nine sessions through Wednesday. Spot bitcoin ETFs have now erased their net inflows for 2026.

Crypto trading generates transaction revenue for Robinhood, so lower volume generally means fewer fees, even when assets on the platform keep growing. The company reports full fourth-quarter results early next year, and October’s figures are the first look at how the quarter started.

The company has kept expanding its crypto footprint anyway. In October, Robinhood won a license in Dubai to offer bitcoin and stock trading in the Middle East starting in 2027.

Robinhood also said cash and deposit balances fell 20% in October to $16.4 billion, mostly because customers were net buyers, and that the decline has largely reversed in early November. November’s operating data will show whether this month’s selloff below $70,000 brought crypto traders back or pushed more of them toward event contracts.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Kraken Parent Payward Breaks Trading Reliance as Services and Custody Drive Q3 Margin
summary:
Kraken parent Payward is decoupling its profitability from the crypto trading cycle. In the third quarter, client assets and enterprise services generated 52% of the group’s core margin, eclipsing trading commissions for the first time.
The Shift from Churn to Custody
The structural shift helped Pay...
content:
2026-11-13T17:21:43.964+02:00

Friday, 13/11/2026 | 15:21 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Client assets and paid access generated 52% of Payward’s Q3 platform margin.
  • Payward expanded its business beyond Kraken trading through Reap’s payments infrastructure and custody services for WOO X EU.

Kraken parent Payward is decoupling its profitability from the crypto trading cycle. In the third quarter, client assets and enterprise services generated 52% of the group’s core margin, eclipsing trading commissions for the first time.

The Shift from Churn to Custody

The structural shift helped Payward nearly triple its adjusted EBITDA to $60 million from $23 million in the second quarter, even as platform trading volumes remained 30% below year-earlier levels.

While trade matching remains central to Kraken’s brand, transaction fees no longer form the majority of what the company retains from its operations.

Payward’s newly adopted performance metric, Total Platform Margin (TPM), captures this shift. It replaces the traditional "adjusted revenue" line and measures net intake after deducting direct trading costs and the staking yields paid out to clients.

For Q3, TPM reached $487 million, up 12% quarter-on-quarter, though still trailing Q3 2025 by 12%. The recovery came from asset-based margin, service and access fees and transaction margin.

Assembling the B2B Infrastructure Ecosystem

The group is now focused on packaging its custody, settlement, and liquidity rails for third parties, as opposed to onboarding retail customers.

This shift from a retail crypto venue into a multi-asset infrastructure provider is reflected on Payward’s Q3 balance sheet During the quarter, Payward closed its acquisition of Reap, adding enterprise card issuance and payment rails.

In September, rival broker WOO X launched its European operations powered directly by Payward Services’ custody and backend. Simultaneously, a partnership with the London Stock Exchange laid the groundwork to bring UK-listed shares onto Payward’s tokenised xStocks platform.

Following the close of Q3, Payward agreed to acquire the parent of Lithuania-based Saldo Bank. Pending regulatory approvals through 2027, the deal will allow Payward to take European customer deposits directly onto its own regulated balance sheet..

title: Kalshi Ends Trump Jr. Advisory Role After 1789 Capital Invests in Rival Polymarket
summary:
Key Takeaways: Kalshi terminated its partnership with Donald Trump Jr.’s firm after it made a bet on their competitor, Polymarket. The conversations started in August, with 1789 Capital rising in
The post Kalshi Ends Trump Jr. Advisory Role After 1789 Capital Invests in Rival Polymarket appeared fir...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Kalshi terminated its partnership with Donald Trump Jr.’s firm after it made a bet on their competitor, Polymarket.
  • The conversations started in August, with 1789 Capital rising in Polymarket’s newest round.
  • That’s an outcome that seems to coincide with rising interest by U.S. lawmakers in predicting markets.

Kalshi has terminated its partnership with Donald Trump Jr. after his investment company 1789 Capital invested in rival Polymarket. The shift follows heightened inquiries about political ties and regulation by prediction market sites.

  • 1789 Capital’s Investment Creates a Conflict
  • Trump Jr. Held Stakes in Both Companies
    • Prediction Markets Face Greater Political Scrutiny
    • US Lawmakers Target Insider Trading

1789 Capital’s Investment Creates a Conflict

A Kalshi spokesperson confirmed to Reuters on November 12 that both sides had agreed to end Trump Jr.’s advisory role after his firm made a significant investment in a rival platform.

Discussions about ending the contract began in August, when 1789 Capital led Polymarket’s latest funding round. In the fall, Kalshi reached out to Trump Jr. about the possible conflict of interest.

The company expressed its gratitude for his contribution to marketing Kalshi and making it customer friendly. And didn’t accept train companies’ political pressure, it added.

Read More: 22 Companies Block OKXICE Tokenized Stocks, Putting 63-Share Crypto Plan Under Pressure

Trump Jr. Held Stakes in Both Companies

In January 2025, Trump Jr. signed on as a strategic adviser to Kalshi with an equity stake. At the time, The Financial Times reported that his shares were worth about $300,000.

At Kalshi, the company was competing with 1789 Capital, which was also becoming more involved with Polymarket. Trump Jr. is a partner at the investment firm, which was a big supporter of Kalshi’s competitor.

Polymarket declined to comment to Reuters. A spokesperson for 1789 Capital declined to comment, and Trump Jr. didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

Prediction Markets Face Greater Political Scrutiny

The move coincides with growing interest among US lawmakers in prediction markets. These sites became more widely known in the 2024 presidential race when their predictions eventually became correct as conventional politics appeared to be dodging.

However, their expansion has also raised concerns about insider trading, political influence and the legality of certain event-based contracts.

Some of the Kalshi employees had worries that the firm’s relationship with the president’s son might cause the company to be subjected to congressional probes, Reuters reported. Kalshi said there were no political risks to consider while making the decision.

Read More: JPMorgan Cuts Polymarket Banking Ties Amid Regulatory Concerns and $20B Valuation

US Lawmakers Target Insider Trading

Industry is under fire all around. Senator Elizabeth Warren has asked for an end to insider trading on prediction markets. A bill by Senator Chris Murphy and Representative Greg Casar earlier this year to label betting on military operations and such sensitive government activity as unpatriotic.

In addition, there have been questions about political donations and trades on both Kalshi and Polymarket. A succession of out-of-sync wagers has raised the spectre of some wagers being based on insider knowledge.

Kalshi’s move further deepens a crack in a sector that is increasingly being questioned on its operations and the number of people allowed to trade on it.

title: President Trump Taps Two Democrats in Bipartisan Slate of SEC and CFTC Nominees as Both Agencies Run Short-Handed
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

President Trump Taps Two Democrats in Bipartisan Slate of SEC and CFTC Nominees as Both Agencies Run Short-Handed
The White House sent four SEC and CFTC nominees to the Senate on Thursday, including former CFTC Commissioner Kristin Johnson and two staffers who worked on the Clarity...
content:
President Donald Trump sent the Senate four nominees for the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on Thursday, his first picks for either agency in about a year and the first Democrats he has put forward for them.

Former CFTC Commissioner Kristin Johnson, a Democrat, and Republican Steven Levine were nominated to the SEC. Republican Nathan Anonick and Democrat Matthew Rowland were nominated to the CFTC, Bloomberg Law reported.

Each nominee needs Senate confirmation. The Senate Banking Committee will handle the SEC picks, while the Senate Agriculture Committee will take up the CFTC pair before any vote by the full chamber.

Who the nominees are

Levine was tapped for the SEC seat left by Hester Peirce, whose term expired, for a term running through June 5, 2030. He most recently served as general counsel and a senior adviser at the White House Council of Economic Advisers and previously worked at the SEC as counsel and deputy chief of staff to Commissioner Mark Uyeda.

Peirce led the SEC’s Crypto Task Force and was one of the agency’s most vocal supporters of clearer crypto rules.

Johnson would take the seat formerly held by Democrat Caroline Crenshaw, for a term ending June 5, 2029. She served as a CFTC commissioner until 2025 and is a former law school professor. During her time at the CFTC, she spoke often about digital assets, including custody and decentralized finance.

Both CFTC nominees come from the Senate Agriculture Committee, which oversees the derivatives regulator. Anonick is legislative counsel to Chairman John Boozman and was a lead negotiator on the committee’s portion of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act. He was nominated to the seat once held by former Chairman Rostin Behnam, for a term ending June 19, 2031.

Rowland is a CFTC attorney detailed to the committee who also worked on the Clarity Act and the committee’s 2024 crypto bill. He previously served on Johnson’s staff at the CFTC, according to his LinkedIn profile. He would fill the remainder of former Commissioner Summer Mersinger’s term, which expires April 13, 2028.

Both agencies can seat up to five commissioners, with no more than three from one party. The SEC currently has two, Chairman Paul Atkins and Commissioner Mark Uyeda. Chairman Mike Selig is the CFTC’s only sitting commissioner.

Lame-duck timing and a Democratic Senate

The timing puts the nominees in front of a Senate in its lame-duck session, weeks after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterms. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, one of crypto’s sharpest critics, is expected to chair the Banking Committee when the new Congress is seated in January.

The pairing of Democrats with Republicans could matter for confirmation. After the election, TD Cowen’s Jaret Seiberg told clients he did not expect Democrats to confirm Trump nominees unless the president filled Democratic seats at agencies such as the SEC, a step he called unlikely. Thursday’s slate does exactly that at both regulators.

The nominations also land with crypto market structure legislation stalled. The Clarity Act failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15 and dies on Jan. 3 unless the lame-duck session revives it.

Without new law, the SEC and CFTC have set crypto policy largely on their own this year. Selig’s CFTC opened the door to equity perpetual futures, and a federal judge later said the agency likely overstepped while letting trading continue.

The White House did not say when it expects the Senate to act. The open question is whether a Senate heading for Democratic control moves the four nominees before January, or leaves the SEC and CFTC running with skeleton commissions into 2027.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Bitcoin Price Briefly Crashes to $67,500, Lowest Since August, as Dollar Holds 19-Month High
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Briefly Crashes to $67,500, Lowest Since August, as Dollar Holds 19-Month High
Bitcoin price briefly crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern, its lowest level since August, then recovered near $69,800 on Friday after October producer prices rose less than exp...
content:
Bitcoin price traded near $69,800 on Friday morning after briefly crashing to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern, its lowest level since mid-August, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The rebound held after October producer prices rose less than economists had expected, though the U.S. dollar remained near a 19-month high and traders still fully priced a December Federal Reserve rate hike.

Bitcoin price was trading near $72,800 at this time Thursday. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then gave way late at night, breaking below $70,000 and sliding to that midnight low. The move also pushed the bitcoin price below its 200-week moving average, a long-term trend line near $68,000. Buyers lifted it back above $69,000 before sunrise, and the rebound extended toward $69,800 after the producer-price report.

A stronger dollar and higher yields weigh on the bitcoin price

The U.S. Dollar Index held above 103 Friday after a three-day rally took it to its highest level since April 2025. The 10-year Treasury yield was near 5.15% ahead of the data, and two-year yields, which track Fed expectations most closely, were on pace for their worst week since 2024, Bloomberg reported.

Traders still see an 88% chance of a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting and a 12% chance of a half-point move, CME FedWatch data show. Fed Governor Christopher Waller has added a 50-basis-point increase to the discussion, and New York Fed President John Williams said Thursday that inflation remains high and policymakers need to take further action.

Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar tends to drain demand for risk assets. Both have pressured the bitcoin price since this week’s hotter-than-expected consumer price index.

Bitcoin has also broken from tech stocks. It fell 5.9% between Nov. 5 and Nov. 12 while the Nasdaq 100 gained 6.4%, a sign it is trading more on yields and the dollar than on the AI trade. Nasdaq 100 futures were up about 0.6% Friday after the producer-price report, as investors also weighed Nvidia’s announcement that Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO.

Leverage unwinds and ETF selling continues

The break below $70,000 set off a wave of forced selling. About $1.64 billion in crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, with bets on higher prices making up nearly 89% of the total and bitcoin positions accounting for $916 million.

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs added to the pressure. The funds posted about $47.7 million in net outflows Thursday, their sixth straight day of withdrawals, bringing the run to roughly $1.49 billion. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) alone bled about $2 billion over nine sessions through Wednesday, and the group has now flipped to about $1.56 billion in net outflows for 2026.

Sentiment has soured with it. A widely watched crypto fear and greed gauge dropped to 20 Friday, its lowest reading since July 8, and bitcoin is now on track for a second straight down year.

Positioning has turned defensive. Average perpetual futures funding rates turned negative for the first time in a month as the price fell toward $68,500, meaning short sellers are now paying to hold their bets. Order books are also thin. Bitcoin order-book depth across major exchanges fell to $72 million on Nov. 9, roughly 33% below normal levels. “Liquidity remains thin while leverage stays elevated, leaving the market vulnerable to sharp moves in either direction,” said Tanay Ved, a senior research associate at Talos.

Producer prices rise less than expected

The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% monthly increase economists had expected, after a revised 1.4% advance in September. Core prices, which exclude food and energy, increased 0.3%, matching forecasts. On an unadjusted basis, the headline index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler report took some pressure off the dollar, which still held above 103, but a December rate hike remains fully priced, leaving limited relief for the bitcoin price heading into the weekend.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $69,800.
