title: Arthur Hayes ‘flattered’ as Coinbase backs US stock perps
summary: Arthur Hayes said he was “flattered” by Coinbase’s defense of US stock perpetual futures, a decade after BitMEX launched perpetual swaps.
content:
Arthur Hayes, co-founder of BitMEX, said he was “flattered” by Coinbase’s support for the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in a US legal dispute over stock perpetual futures.

“When we launched the perpetual swap at BitMEX in 2016, Washington’s reaction was less than warm,” Hayes told Cointelegraph. “Ten years later, Coinbase is in federal court defending the right to offer them on US stocks. I’m flattered. Imitation is the sincerest form of regulation.”

Coinbase and five other companies submitted a brief on Monday opposing the alliance’s request to block trading in perpetual futures tied to individual stocks. The court accepted the brief on Tuesday.

The Capital Markets Alliance Association (CMAA), which brought the lawsuit, says the contracts should be treated as security-based swaps, which face tighter restrictions on retail trading.

Hayes was CEO of BitMEX when the crypto derivatives exchange launched its Bitcoin perpetual swap, which let traders take leveraged positions on Bitcoin without a fixed expiration date. The product helped make perpetual swaps a staple of crypto trading.

SEC weighs in on stock perpetuals

The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) reportedly submitted a proposed court brief on Monday, opposing the alliance’s request to temporarily halt trading in the contracts.

The agency said it was reviewing the exchanges’ rules for listing the contracts. The brief left open whether the SEC would set those rules aside and whether the contracts qualify as security futures or security-based swaps.

Related: EU DeFi proposals could push users to riskier platforms, says Coinbase exec

In a Tuesday court filing, CMAA said that the CFTC had approved the contracts without adequately explaining its decision or addressing unresolved regulatory questions.

The group also cited about $375 million in reported 24-hour notional trading volume for Kalshi’s stock perpetuals shortly after launch, claiming the products were already diverting business from traditional stock markets.

Stock perpetuals’ lack of expiry is at issue

Stock perpetuals let traders speculate on individual share prices without owning the underlying stocks. Unlike traditional futures, the contracts have no fixed expiration date.

On Nov. 3, US District Judge Valerie Caproni denied the group’s request for a temporary restraining order because it had yet to show likely irreparable harm. She found the alliance was likely to succeed on its claim that the CFTC exceeded its authority.

Wojciech Kaszycki, strategy adviser to BTCS SA, said the lack of a fixed expiration or delivery date could complicate the case for treating perpetual contracts as futures.

Kaszycki told Cointelegraph that the case “sale for future delivery.”

However, he warned that a ruling against the CFTC could push trading activity toward offshore and decentralized platforms.

“The product doesn’t die; it just changes address,” he said.

Friday, 13/11/2026 | 13:09 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • The firm has yet to launch products or services under its new UAE license.
  • Recently, Capital.com, Equiti and XTB also secured UAE brokerage authorisations.

VCG Markets has secured a Category One license from the United Arab Emirates' Capital Market Authority, authorising its local entity to offer OTC derivatives and spot currency trading.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The approval comes as more international brokers expand their regulated operations in the UAE. The number of firms authorised for OTC derivatives and spot forex trading in the country has increased from 11 to 28. Capital.com and Equiti have also secured Category One licenses, while XTB obtained Category One and Category Two authorisations to expand its local brokerage operations.

UAE Entity Appoints New Compliance and MLRO Head

The license was granted to VCG Securities Financial Consultation LLC. The approval follows the group's efforts to establish its business in the UAE as part of its regional strategy.

In October, VCG Markets appointed Mohammed Chouikh as Head of Compliance and Money Laundering Reporting Officer at the UAE entity.

Commenting on the license, Brian Myers, Group CEO of VCG Markets, said: “Securing the Category One license is a natural progression for VCG Markets. We have established roots in the UAE, and this step reflects the commitment we've made to the region.”

He said the company's priority was to continue developing its UAE business with a focus on long-term growth.

VCG Markets Clarifies Scope of UAE License

The authorization applies only to VCG Securities Financial Consultation LLC and the activities covered by its license. It does not extend to other companies operating under the VCG Markets brand or change their existing regulatory arrangements.

No products or services are currently available under the new license. VCG Markets said it would announce any future offerings separately, along with details of their availability and applicable regulatory framework.

The group operates in more than 80 countries. However, it has yet to announce when it plans to launch services under the new UAE authorization.

title: Michael Burry Says ‘Get Out’ of Nvidia Stock as Jensen Huang’s Sudden Exit Sparks Chaos
summary: Michael Burry has urged Nvidia investors to sell their shares, arguing Jensen Huang’s sudden resignation could weaken the relationships underpinning the chipmaker’s AI expansion.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: NVDA

Michael Burry has urged Nvidia investors to sell their shares, arguing Jensen Huang’s sudden resignation could weaken the relationships underpinning the chipmaker’s AI expansion.

The warning came on November 12, shortly after Nvidia confirmed that its longtime CEO had stepped down with immediate effect. Burry believes Huang’s departure could expose weaknesses in the company’s customer relationships, financing arrangements, and growth strategy, potentially putting further pressure on NVDA shares.

Burry, the investor known for predicting the 2008 US housing market collapse depicted in The Big Short, outlined several reasons for his bearish outlook in a Substack post. He argued that Huang’s personal influence played an important role in maintaining Nvidia’s commercial ecosystem and that his absence could change how customers and business partners approach the company.

Michael Burry Warns Nvidia Investors About Customer Relationships and Financing Risks

Burry’s central argument focuses on the influence Huang exercised over Nvidia’s customers and business partners. According to the investor, the CEO played an important role in persuading major technology companies and AI infrastructure providers to commit to Nvidia’s hardware, including through arrangements that encouraged customers to purchase chips ahead of their immediate requirements.

Michael Burry urged Nvidia investors to sell, warning that Jensen Huang’s exit could undermine the company’s leadership and growth. Source: @burrytracker/X

Without Huang directing those relationships, Burry believes customers could become more willing to reconsider existing commitments. He argued that companies may now have greater freedom to “slow down deals, push back, renegotiate terms” or switch to competing chip suppliers.

The investor also raised concerns about Nvidia’s financing arrangements. He claimed the company used special-purpose vehicles and other financial structures to help customers fund purchases of its AI chips. In his assessment, these arrangements created “tremendous leverage in the system” by connecting Nvidia’s chip sales, customer financing, and broader investments in the artificial intelligence industry.

Burry suggested that Huang’s departure could disrupt this interconnected structure. If customers reduce purchases or reconsider their financing commitments, some investments supporting the AI ecosystem could lose momentum. He also warned that existing arrangements might take considerable time to unwind, potentially affecting cash flows across the industry.

Another concern involves Nvidia’s chip allocation strategy. Burry alleged that Huang encouraged customers to purchase hardware before they immediately needed it, partly by warning that future allocations could be reduced if they delayed their orders. Without the founder overseeing these relationships, customers may feel less pressure to accept the same commercial terms.

However, these arguments represent Burry’s interpretation of Nvidia’s business model rather than established findings of financial misconduct. The implications of the financing arrangements and customer commitments will depend on how the company manages them under its new leadership.

Burry ultimately acknowledged that Nvidia’s underlying business would not disappear following Huang’s departure. Nevertheless, he believes its growth could slow, and its profit margins could come under pressure if customers gain more negotiating power. He concluded his warning with a direct message to investors: “Nvidia bulls will have another fluffy big chance to get out. Get out.”

Nvidia Stock Recovers After Sharp Sell-Off Following Huang’s Resignation

Nvidia shares experienced significant volatility after the company announced Huang’s departure. The sudden leadership change added another layer of uncertainty to an already difficult period for the AI chipmaker, with investors reassessing the potential consequences for its business strategy and future growth.

NVDA price chart. Source: TradingView

NVDA fell sharply during early trading on November 12, reaching an intraday low of $148.80. This represented a decline of approximately 14.3% from the previous closing price of $173.73. However, buyers emerged later in the session, allowing the stock to recover part of its losses.

Nvidia ultimately closed at $166.19 on November 12, down 4.34% for the session. The decline reduced the company’s market capitalization by approximately $180 billion, bringing its valuation to around $4.01 trillion. Trading activity also surged, with more than 740 million shares changing hands during the session.

As of the latest available overnight market update on November 13, NVDA was quoted at approximately $166.38, according to Yahoo Finance. The regular-session closing price remains $166.19, as the November 13 trading session had yet to begin at the time of the update.

The decline also extended a broader weakness in Nvidia shares. The stock had already retreated from its early-October high of approximately $243, reflecting pressure across AI-related equities and concerns about the scale and sustainability of artificial intelligence investment.

Market participants are now evaluating whether Nvidia can maintain its commercial influence without its founder. The transition could affect customer negotiations, strategic partnerships, supply agreements, and the financing arrangements that have helped accelerate AI infrastructure spending.

Colette Kress Takes Over as Nvidia’s Interim CEO

Nvidia confirmed Huang’s immediate resignation on November 12, ending his tenure as the company’s chief executive, president, and board member. The announcement followed several days of intense scrutiny surrounding reports of alleged extramarital relationships and concerns about a possible foreign intelligence operation.

Nvidia appoints CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO, effective immediately. Source: @BullTheoryio/X

Huang had acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in a message to employees earlier in November. Separately, Nvidia’s board announced an independent investigation into reports that he may have been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The company stated that it had no reason to believe its trade secrets or national security interests had been compromised.

Importantly, the allegations surrounding the suspected Chinese intelligence connection remain unresolved. On November 12, US Attorney General Todd Blanche said the Justice Department had not reached a conclusion about whether Alice Huang, the businesswoman linked to the allegations, was working for the Chinese government. Beijing has also denied the espionage claims.

Following the CEO transition, Nvidia appointed longtime Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim chief executive. Kress joined the company in September 2013 and will retain her CFO responsibilities while overseeing the business during the leadership search.

The board also appointed Harvey C. Jones as its first-ever chair. Jones has served on Nvidia’s board since 1993 and brings decades of experience in technology management and venture investing.

Nvidia said it would consider both internal and external candidates for the permanent CEO position. Jones also expressed confidence in Kress and the existing leadership team, stating that the company’s operations, customer commitments, and product roadmap were expected to continue without interruption.

The transition nevertheless creates a difficult challenge. Huang led Nvidia for more than three decades and became closely associated with its expansion from a graphics processor manufacturer into a central supplier of AI computing infrastructure. Replacing his leadership will involve more than appointing another executive. The next CEO will also need to maintain relationships with customers, developers, suppliers, and investors across the global technology industry.

More Than 1,600 Nvidia Employees Call for Jensen Huang’s Return

Despite the controversy surrounding Huang’s departure, the former CEO continues to receive support from parts of Nvidia’s workforce.

A report published by WIRED on November 12 revealed that an internal suggestion-box post urging the board to consider employee sentiment had attracted more than 1,600 comments. Most of the responses reportedly supported bringing Huang back to the company.

More than 1,600 Nvidia employees urged the board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO following his resignation. Source: @BullTheoryio/X

One employee wrote, “If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss,” reflecting the loyalty Huang developed during his decades at the chipmaker.

Another commenter argued that Huang deserved a second chance, writing, “We are all humans and can make mistakes.” The responses indicate that some employees believe his contributions to Nvidia should be considered separately from the personal allegations surrounding his departure.

The internal discussion reportedly began before the resignation was announced. A longtime Nvidia engineer had submitted the original suggestion-box post, asking the board to consider employees’ views before making a decision about Huang’s future.

One employee also sent a companywide email requesting greater transparency about the circumstances surrounding the leadership change. The message expressed continued support for Huang while calling attention to his contribution to the company’s development.

However, the internal comments do not necessarily represent the views of Nvidia’s entire workforce. They do highlight the challenge facing the board as it attempts to manage a leadership transition involving a founder whose influence extends well beyond his formal position.

For investors, the employee response adds another dimension to the uncertainty. Retaining experienced engineers, executives, and other employees will be important as Nvidia works to preserve its technological advantage and maintain its relationships with customers.

Nvidia’s Upcoming Earnings Report Becomes a Key Test for NVDA Investors

Nvidia’s leadership crisis comes just days before its next financial results. The company is scheduled to announce its fiscal third-quarter 2027 results on November 17, with Colette Kress expected to provide the financial commentary in her capacity as CFO.

The report will give investors an opportunity to evaluate Nvidia’s operating performance amid the recent turmoil. Revenue growth, profit margins, customer demand, and management’s outlook for AI infrastructure spending are likely to remain central areas of interest.

Burry’s warning places particular emphasis on the relationship between Nvidia’s growth and the commercial arrangements supporting demand for its chips. Investors will therefore be watching for any indications that customers are changing their purchasing plans or that financing commitments could affect future orders.

Nevertheless, Huang’s resignation does not automatically mean that Nvidia’s technological position or existing customer relationships will deteriorate. The company retains its established product portfolio, engineering workforce, and extensive ecosystem of developers and industry partners.

The immediate challenge is to demonstrate that these advantages can remain intact under different leadership. Kress and the board will need to reassure investors that the company’s commercial strategy can continue without the executive who directed its expansion for 33 years.

For now, Burry’s sell warning reflects concerns about Nvidia’s leadership dependence, customer financing, and future profitability. Whether those risks translate into weaker financial performance remains to be seen. The November 17 earnings announcement and the board’s search for a permanent CEO will provide investors with important developments to assess as NVDA navigates this transition.

But yes, if you run a bigger community, blog, or YouTube channel, you can apply for the MEXC Affiliate Program instead.   • Your MEXC account is more than 30 days old: MEXC currently lets users add a missed referrer after registration only during the first 30 days. So, an account older than 30 days normally cannot use the self-service referral linking option.
  • Another referrer is already connected to your account: MEXC does not let you freely replace an existing referrer with a new referral code. 
  • Country or location restrictions: MEXC does not offer promotional bonuses in certain restricted countries due to some local crypto laws. Hence, if you sign up from a restricted region (like the U.S. or Canada) or use a VPN that changes your location, the promo benefits will not activate.
  • Old browser cookies overwrite your code: You see, your browser stores cookies from older referral links you clicked before. These saved cookies can override the manual code box during registration. You can clear your browser cache or even use an Incognito tab to solve this issue.

Can I Use a MEXC Referral Code After Registering My Account?

Yes, MEXC now allows eligible users to link a referral code after account registration, provided the account was created within the past 30 days and meets some of the linking rules.

The current “Self-Service Referrer Linking” feature lets an eligible main account enter a referral code or referrer UID after sign-up. But the account must be less than 30 days old. Plus, sub-accounts are not supported for this feature, and the selected referrer must have created their MEXC account before you created yours.

You can therefore try adding “mexc-bestbonus” through the self-service linking page during that 30-day window.

But again, there is one catch. Linking a referrer later does not automatically mean every expired registration task or promotional benefit will be restored. Generally, some new-user campaigns track eligibility from the original registration time. So, we suggest you enter the “mexc-bestbonus” code during initial registration only.

What Are the Typical Types of MEXC Bonuses?

The different types of MEXC bonuses are Futures Bonuses, Copy Trade Bonuses, Prediction Markets Bonuses, Spot or Deposit Bonuses, Fee Vouchers, and New User Sign-Up Bonuses.

Futures Bonus

A MEXC Futures Bonus is a trading bonus that you can use for eligible futures trading instead of using only your own money. MEXC lets you use a futures bonus for USDT-M futures trading. The bonus can help cover trading fees, funding fees, and trading losses. Also, it can work as margin when your available USDT balance is not enough.

Well, the important part is that the bonus itself cannot be withdrawn, but profits made from bonus-supported trades can be withdrawn. You should also avoid moving assets out of your “Futures Wallet” while you still have an unused futures bonus. Actually, under MEXC’s current rules, doing this can eventually cause the remaining bonus to be removed from your account.

Copy Trade Bonus

A MEXC copy trade bonus is a special trial fund made for futures copy trading. Copy trading lets you follow another trader and then automatically copy eligible trades. MEXC gives copy trade bonuses through its “Rewards Hub” to new users during promotions and special copy trading events.

The copy trade bonus can also help cover eligible fees, losses, and funding fees from copy trading. But again, you cannot transfer the bonus out of the “Copy Trading” account or withdraw it as normal USDT. Plus, any unused amount will also disappear after its expiry date.

Prediction Markets Bonus

MEXC Prediction Markets allow you to predict the results of selected events. You can trade “YES or NO” contracts tied to real-world events, including sports outcomes and crypto price levels. The exchange will provide prediction market bonuses through special campaigns.

The main benefit is simple. You use the bonus for an eligible prediction only. Your real account balance is not used for the bonus amount. Here, if your bonus prediction wins, the profit is credited as real funds and can normally be withdrawn. But, on the other hand, if your prediction loses, you lose the bonus used for that prediction rather than the same amount from your real assets.

Spot / Deposit Bonus

A MEXC Spot or Deposit Bonus is usually an event reward you will receive after making a qualifying deposit, holding funds, or completing spot trading tasks. 

You should pay attention to the words net deposit. MEXC normally calculates it as your total eligible deposits minus your withdrawals during the event. Therefore, depositing 500 USDT and then withdrawing most of it may stop you from meeting a 500 USDT net deposit requirement.

Fee Vouchers

Fee vouchers directly cut down what you pay in trading costs, rather than adding new funds to your account balance. Here, our “mexc-bestbonus” referral code gives you a flat 10% discount on spot and futures fees for as long as your account stays active on the platform. 

Also, some task-based vouchers exist separately too, covering a fixed dollar amount of fees for a limited stretch of time after you claim them.

New User Sign-Up Bonus

A MEXC New User Sign-Up Bonus is a group of welcome rewards offered to eligible users after they create a new account and complete selected tasks.

As discussed above, MEXC currently offers new-user rewards worth up to 10,000 USDT. But again, this does not mean every new account receives 10,000 USDT immediately. Actually, reaching the maximum amount generally requires you to complete several deposit and trading tasks with much higher requirements.

What Are the Best Alternatives to the MEXC Referral Code (mexc-bestbonus) in 2026?

The best alternatives to the “mexc-bestbonus” referral code are the Binance code (P8DEY0JB), Bybit code (CNJREFERRAL), OKX code (CNJREFCODE), and Bitget code (ew9a68), if you prefer offers on other exchanges.

  • Binance (P8DEY0JB): Binance offers up to $100 in welcome rewards plus a 10% lifetime discount on trading fees when you use this code. The tasks are very simple: just KYC, a $10 deposit, and one trade worth $10. Compared with Binance, MEXC gives broader cryptocurrency trading access through more trading pairs. This makes it one of the easiest bonuses on this list to actually finish in full.
  • Bybit (CNJREFERRAL): Bybit runs one of the largest bonus pools around; 30,020 USDT spread across eight separate tiers.   • OKX (CNJREFCODE): OKX offers up to 10,000 USDT in welcome rewards along with a 30% permanent fee discount. Overview of the MEXC Affiliate Program

The MEXC Global affiliate offering on the MEXC trading platform lets you make money by sharing your invite link, and affiliates can earn passive income when active traders they refer keep trading. When people sign up with your link and trade, you get a cut of their trading fees from both spot and futures markets, with commissions driven by the trading activity of new traders. You usually start with a 50% commission, but this can go up to 70%, plus 10% sub-affiliate rewards. The MEXC referral program offers tracking tools, and MEXC offers affiliates a broader set of partner benefits.

This program is mainly made for crypto creators, community leaders, influencers, websites, and marketing teams. Strong security features, including cold storage and two factor authentication, also help build trust. Now, along with regular commissions, partners can even get monthly Kickstarter airdrops, special event invites, and 24/7 customer support. It can also suit those looking for passive income. title: Chainstack Traces Customer Data Breach to Exposed Admin Tools
summary: The expanded report shows why replacing a password is only one part of recovery, alongside node credentials, application changes and access controls.
content:
TL;DR: Chainstack’s expanded incident report focuses on access-control failures. Its recovery guidance makes completed credential rotation a priority.

Chainstack has added technical detail to the security incident it first disclosed on November 3. Its updated report, with a technical section dated November 10, describes an October intrusion built around configuration and access-control failures. The company says it found no evidence that a software vulnerability was exploited.

How the access controls failed

According to Chainstack, the attacker entered through a development Grafana instance with unchanged default administrator credentials. An unauthenticated tool server with broad Kubernetes permissions then formed part of the access path. Machine credentials also connected the development and production environments.

The operational lesson is about the reach of an account after the first login. A low-profile testing service can become consequential if it can contact sensitive systems or holds privileges that extend beyond its immediate job.

NewsBTC's coverage of the NEAR AI infrastructure incident explored a related boundary between an application and the services supporting it. The mechanisms differ, but both make the surrounding infrastructure relevant to a crypto platform's security.

What customers are being asked to address

The report identifies account names, organisation details, email addresses and password hashes as potentially exposed. It treats node credentials as exposed despite finding no evidence they were read, and asks customers to change passwords, rotate node credentials and regenerate platform API keys where used.

A password hash and a working access token create different problems. Hashes are representations of passwords, while an active token may directly authorise requests. Replacing a login password therefore cannot be assumed to invalidate every other credential associated with an application.

This is why incident guidance needs to identify the affected credential types clearly. A single instruction to change a password can leave developers uncertain about application endpoints, automated jobs and service integrations.

Credential rotation has a completion step

Chainstack's node-management documentation describes a staged rotation process. New credentials are generated while the existing ones remain active. Applications can then move to the replacements before the old credentials are deactivated.

The documentation says both sets continue working until that final step, with no automatic time limit. Completing the rotation permanently rejects requests using the previous credentials. It also says a node rotation does not change a multichain authentication token.

For an operator, the overlap reduces the risk of interrupting a working service while updating applications. The corresponding responsibility is to finish the migration. Generating a replacement alone leaves the previous means of access available.

A useful completion record would therefore track which applications have moved and when the old credentials were disabled. That is a practical control a team can verify after the initial emergency.

The underlying design problem is familiar

Grafana's security guidance warns that services on its local network may be reachable through its data-source proxy. It describes controls such as limiting permitted destinations and using firewall rules to restrict access to sensitive internal services.

Those precautions address what a tool can reach, as well as who can log into it. Authentication and network boundaries perform different jobs; permission limits provide another layer if either boundary fails.

NewsBTC's report on Chainalysis restoring screening services shows why operational recovery and data-exposure analysis can follow different timelines.

Chainstack's expanded account gives customers more detail to assess. The remaining test is whether access changes are completed and whether the revised controls can prevent one compromised service from reaching far beyond its intended role.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: The Future of Prop Trading: Broker Licenses & IB Deals
summary: Prop trading firms face a strategic choice: continue refining the challenge-based model or move closer to regulated brokerage through licences and introducing broker partnerships. As acquisition costs and payout economics come under pressure, the sustainability of each route deserves closer examinat...
content:
2026-11-13T11:43:33.016+02:00

Friday, 13/11/2026 | 09:43 GMT by FM Events

  • Examine whether prop trading firms can build sustainable businesses through broker licensing, IB partnerships and new operating models.

Prop trading firms face a strategic choice: continue refining the challenge-based model or move closer to regulated brokerage through licences and introducing broker partnerships. As acquisition costs and payout economics come under pressure, the sustainability of each route deserves closer examination.

Challenge pricing, acquisition costs, payouts and retention all shape whether the model can last.

This discussion brings together prop firm operators, retail brokers, and the providers serving both to examine which of prop trading's possible futures is actually being built. Finance Magnates Summit London 2026 brings prop firm operators and brokerage specialists together at Old Billingsgate on 24 November to examine the licensing, partnership and commercial decisions behind these models.

Prop trading is being reshaped by commercial pressures as much as by regulation. Challenge pricing, trader acquisition, payouts and churn all influence whether an operator can build a sustainable business. The conversation in London will look beyond the headline growth story to the economics that determine which models survive.

One potential direction is closer integration with retail brokerage. Some firms are examining broker licences, introducing broker arrangements and hybrid models that connect trading challenges to regulated services. Each option surfaces new questions about operating costs, risk management, client journeys and the division of responsibilities between partners.

For prop operators, brokers and service providers, the value of the discussion lies in understanding what is changing in practice. Which partnerships create durable commercial value? When does licensing make sense from a strategic standpoint? And how should businesses assess the trade-offs between scale, control and complexity? The session will put these decisions into a broader industry context.

Join the session at 10:10 - 10:50 on 24 November and explore the full agenda at: https://events.financemagnates.com/events/fmsummitlondon/agenda/schedule

A viable prop trading strategy depends on more than attracting a large number of applicants. Operators need a clear view of trader behaviour, the cost of acquiring and retaining customers and the obligations created when a model starts to resemble regulated brokerage.

For firms exploring a different commercial structure, Finance Magnates Summit London provides an opportunity to speak directly with brokers, platform providers and potential partners.

title: AI & Trading 2027: From Copilots to Colleagues
summary: AI is moving beyond assisting trading teams toward systems capable of carrying out increasingly complex tasks. But before brokers can rely on autonomous tools, they must answer difficult questions about data quality, permissions and accountability. Those are the practical challenges at the heart of ...
content:
2026-11-13T11:30:31.446+02:00

Friday, 13/11/2026 | 09:30 GMT by Finance Magnates

  • Explore how AI is moving from support tools to operational agents and the controls trading firms need before deploying them.

AI is moving beyond assisting trading teams toward systems capable of carrying out increasingly complex tasks. But before brokers can rely on autonomous tools, they must answer difficult questions about data quality, permissions and accountability. Those are the practical challenges at the heart of the AI & Trading 2027 discussion.

The practical challenge is the quality of the data feeding these tools and the controls governing how they act.

The firms building the next AI infrastructure and the brokers buying it compare what has reached production and what needs to be fixed first. At Finance Magnates Summit London 2026, this discussion will examine how firms move from demonstrations to systems they can trust.

The question is no longer whether artificial intelligence belongs in trading operations. It is whether firms can deploy systems that act reliably when the underlying data, permissions and accountability are under pressure. A capable model is only one part of that equation. Data provenance, governance and traceability determine whether an AI-assisted process can move from an impressive demonstration to a dependable business tool.

The discussion will examine where firms should build proprietary capabilities and where external providers can offer a more practical route. Brokers must also consider what happens after deployment: how an agent is identified, how decisions are recorded, who intervenes when outputs are questionable and how controls operate in real time. These questions affect technology, compliance and trading teams alike.

For decision-makers evaluating AI investments for 2027, the session offers a useful way to distinguish operational progress from marketing claims. Expect a discussion of execution analytics, the role of automation and the skills organisations will need as routine work changes. The commercial opportunity is significant, but so is the need to demonstrate that the systems are fit for purpose.

Join the session at 10:10 - 10:50 on 24 November, and explore the full agenda:
https://events.financemagnates.com/events/fmsummitlondon/agenda/schedule

For trading businesses, the practical test of AI is not how convincingly a system can demonstrate a capability, but whether its decisions can be traced, challenged and controlled. Leaders considering deployment need to understand the quality of their data, who owns each decision and what happens when the model produces an unexpected outcome.

The session is also a useful starting point for conversations beyond the conference room. Attendees can compare implementation priorities with technology providers and peers across the exhibition, then use the Summit to identify which partnerships or internal capabilities merit closer examination.

With the summit being less than 2 weeks away, now is the time to secure your place: https://events.financemagnates.com/events/fmsummitlondon/register

title: Binance Puts New Reserve Snapshot Under Scrutiny After $6.3B Crypto Hack
summary:
Key Takeaways: Binance states that assets affected by the hack of $6.3B are covered. There is now a new Proof of Reserves snapshot. The protection of the zero-knowledge proof is
The post Binance Puts New Reserve Snapshot Under Scrutiny After $6.3B Crypto Hack appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Binance states that assets affected by the hack of $6.3B are covered.
  • There is now a new Proof of Reserves snapshot.
  • The protection of the zero-knowledge proof is not yet confirmed.

Weeks after one of the biggest crypto exchange security incidents in history, Binance has just hit a significant recovery landmark. The exchange says affected assets are now fully covered and has released a fresh reserve snapshot to support its backing claims.

  • Binance Finishes Replacing Assets Hit in $6.3B Security Breach
  • New Proof of Reserves Covers 198 Crypto Assets
    • Zero-Knowledge Proof Still Needs to Be Generated
    • Proof of Reserves Adds Transparency, but Its Scope Has Limits

Binance Finishes Replacing Assets Hit in $6.3B Security Breach

Binance stated it has finished covering assets impacted by the security incident on October 29, leading to stolen funds of about $6.3 billion.

The exchange had invested over $6.34 billion of its own money to offset losses as opposed to passing them along to customers. It was divided into three funding streams: some funds from Secure Asset Fund for Users, or SAFU, the surplus funds from their Futures insurance fund and the Binance corporate treasury.

Binance were then restocking cryptocurrencies both through the regular market and via over-the-counter transactions. Recovery was at 90% by Oct. 31 and 98% on Nov. 4, except for less liquid tokens that took a bit longer.

The company also stated that it will be returning the value of SAFU to nearly $1 billion following a part of its Emergency funding during the process.

Read More: Binance Replenishes 98% of $6.34B Hack Losses, Expands Proof of Reserves to 44 Tokens

New Proof of Reserves Covers 198 Crypto Assets

Binance has made its new Proof of Reserves snapshot at 00:00 UTC on Nov. 12. The new snapshot expands on the 44 assets added to its snapshot last Nov. 4 to 198 tokens. However, the snapshot is not a complete verification process, but rather a publication.

Zero-Knowledge Proof Still Needs to Be Generated

Given the complexity of creating the complete zero-knowledge proof, Binance estimates that the task will take between 40 and 50 hours.

After the finalization, all affected asset holders will be able to determine whether they had shares in the reserve calculation and find the right level of backing (1:1 and above). The integration of zk-SNARK and Merkle trees in Binance enables users to verify their account balances without revealing the specific amounts of assets held by individual users in a public display.

Proof of Reserves Adds Transparency, but Its Scope Has Limits

The reserve update provides another snapshot of how Binance’s reserves look on-chain for Binance users afterward from the hack, but PoR is still not a full valuation of Binance’s finances.

As Binance itself points out, PoR can evidence customer balances and corresponding reserves on a specific date, but it is unable to independently prove solvency or information on all its off-chain obligations.

The U.S. Public Company Accounting Oversight Board has also warned that Proof of Reserves engagements are not the same as financial statement audits and that they might not cover liabilities, borrowed assets, or customer legal rights.

The next big event for Binance users is the full zero-knowledge proof launch; this will make Nov. 12 reserve snapshot verifiable with each user’s time.

title: Sygnum Launches ETH Fund Targeting 8–10% Returns in Ether
summary: Sygnum's new ETH Alpha Fund combines staking with trading strategies. Its return target is measured in ETH, leaving investors exposed to the token's dollar price.
content:
TL;DR: Sygnum has announced an ETH-denominated fund targeting 8–10% annual returns after fees. The target includes staking income, and investors remain exposed to ETH's market price.

Sygnum is pitching a different measure of investment performance: how much Ether an investor owns at the end of the year. In its November 12 announcement, the bank introduced the ETH Alpha Fund, which opened to investors on November 2 and is aimed at professional and qualified investors in approved markets.

The target is measured in ETH

The fund's product page makes two distinctions explicit. Its 8–10% objective is the total portfolio target, including staking. It is also denominated in ETH, so the value of an investment in dollars or another currency continues to move with Ether's price.

That changes how the headline number should be read. As a hypothetical illustration, an investor starting with 100 ETH and achieving an 8% token return would finish with 108 ETH. If the dollar price of Ether fell 20% over the same period, the position's dollar value would still be 13.6% lower.

That example describes arithmetic, not a forecast for the fund. It shows why increasing a token balance and preserving purchasing power are different objectives. The meaning of a successful year depends on which currency the investor uses to measure it.

Staking supplies one source of income

Sygnum says the portfolio combines native staking with options premiums, arbitrage and derivatives carry or funding strategies. The trading component aims to earn returns without relying on a directional call on ETH.

Ethereum's staking documentation explains the underlying distinction. Validators receive rewards for their role in maintaining the network. They can also lose ETH through inactivity penalties or slashing, while using a service provider adds another counterparty to the arrangement.

Trading income has a separate economic source. An options premium compensates the seller for accepting an obligation; an arbitrage strategy depends on a pricing difference that can be captured after costs. Neither is simply an extra protocol reward.

Combining these activities may diversify the sources of income. It also makes the resulting product more complex to evaluate than a straightforward staking position.

The structure adds custody and liquidity questions

The launch announcement says trading uses Sygnum Protect, keeping collateral off exchanges at the bank. The product page lists a minimum subscription of $100,000 or its ETH equivalent, monthly subscriptions and monthly redemptions, with advance notice requirements. It also lists an investor-level gate of up to 10%, although the page does not explain its mechanics.

Those terms matter for an institution that must meet cash demands on a different timetable. A quoted asset value does not necessarily mean that capital can be withdrawn immediately. A treasury evaluating such a structure has to match its investment horizon with the fund's dealing arrangements.

Custody deserves the same attention. NewsBTC's coverage of Sygnum's MultiSYG lending arrangement illustrates how the control of collateral can be designed separately from the financial exposure attached to it.

Performance will need more than a yield headline

This launch sits within the broader expansion of institutional ETH products, alongside developments such as Amundi's Ethereum-based fund share class. The products serve different purposes, even though both use Ethereum-related infrastructure.

For the new fund, the useful evidence will be realised returns, the consistency of those returns and how its strategies behave when market conditions change. Comparisons also need the same accounting basis: net with net, ETH with ETH and equivalent observation periods.

An annual target gives investors an objective to assess. A live track record will show how closely the fund can follow it.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Prop Firm FTMO Plans 300 Hires, Half of Them at Its Broker OANDA
summary:
FTMO plans to hire about 300 people over the next 14 months, roughly half for teams at OANDA, which it acquired last year. Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer Marek Vašíček outlined the plan to Czech outlet CzechCrunch today (Friday).
About two-thirds of the roles are technical, according to the...
content:
2026-11-13T10:45:21.131+02:00

Friday, 13/11/2026 | 08:45 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • Two-thirds of the roles are technical, and the broker’s new staff will be recruited in Prague.
  • The company says AI raises the need for people, while eToro and IronFX cut up to 10% of staff.

FTMO plans to hire about 300 people over the next 14 months, roughly half for teams at OANDA, which it acquired last year. Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer Marek Vašíček outlined the plan to Czech outlet CzechCrunch today (Friday).

About two-thirds of the roles are technical, according to the report, and candidates for OANDA's teams will also be hired in Prague. FTMO paid about $422 million for OANDA, partly with a $250 million bank loan, in December 2025.

The group has about 400 staff at FTMO and about 600 at OANDA, so the plan would expand its workforce by roughly 30%. FTMO alone had more than 300 employees when it marked its 10th anniversary with over $450 million paid to traders in September 2025.

The plan runs against the direction of the trading industry. In an Acuiti survey for the second quarter of 2026, 44% of institutional proprietary trading firms said AI was slowing their hiring, and 15% had cut headcount because of it.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Brokers Cut Up to 10% of Staff as FTMO Adds Nearly a Third

Vašíček said the more FTMO can do with AI, the more people it needs.

AI "won't tell us what to build, and it isn't responsible for it," he said.

Retail brokers that announced layoffs this year sized them at no more than a tenth of their workforce, and AI featured in at least two of the explanations.

eToro cut about 7% of its global staff in January, and IronFX cut about 150 of its roughly 1,500 jobs in March. eToro said it was using process automation and AI to operate more efficiently, while sources cited efficiency amid the AI wave at IronFX.

FP Markets reduced its global workforce by less than 7% in April. By FinanceMagnates.com's calculation, FTMO's plan would add about three times as many people, relative to the group's size, as IronFX removed.

OANDA Takes Half the New Roles

Half of the hiring targets OANDA, where the founders have already changed the management since the takeover.

Vašíček and co-founder Otakar Šuffner have run OANDA as co-CEOs since Gavin Bambury stepped down in March. Vašíček said they parted ways with several people after the takeover and are now strengthening existing teams.

He also said OANDA does not offer everything it could in many of its markets. Its estimated trading volume fell 10% quarter-over-quarter in the third quarter of 2026, FM Intelligence's broker volumes tracker shows.

AI Spending in the Millions, Listing Not Ruled Out

FTMO is looking for experienced hires, including AI specialists and product engineers who use AI to take a feature from brief to launch, CzechCrunch reported. A two-day sprint at the Prague office replaces the usual three interview rounds, with a decision within 24 hours.

FTMO spends millions of dollars a year on AI and has direct contracts with Anthropic and Google, according to the report. It has automated content, translations and invoicing.

FTMO plans four product launches next year and is building out futures, which it opened to traders in beta in August, according to CzechCrunch.

The group reported 2025 revenue of about $420 million, up 31%, while net income fell 59% to roughly $37.5 million, the founders told FinanceMagnates.com in October. In that interview, Šuffner did not rule out a stock market listing.

"An FTMO ticker sounds really cool," he said.

Vašíček told CzechCrunch the idea has no concrete outline yet. Two CFD brokers pursued public listings in the first quarter of 2026, the most listing activity in the sector since Plus500's 2013 debut, according to FM Intelligence.

About two-thirds of the roles are technical, according to the report, and candidates for OANDA's teams will also be hired in Prague. FTMO paid about $422 million for OANDA, partly with a $250 million bank loan, in December 2025.

The group has about 400 staff at FTMO and about 600 at OANDA, so the plan would expand its workforce by roughly 30%. FTMO alone had more than 300 employees when it marked its 10th anniversary with over $450 million paid to traders in September 2025.

The plan runs against the direction of the trading industry. In an Acuiti survey for the second quarter of 2026, 44% of institutional proprietary trading firms said AI was slowing their hiring, and 15% had cut headcount because of it.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Brokers Cut Up to 10% of Staff as FTMO Adds Nearly a Third

Vašíček said the more FTMO can do with AI, the more people it needs.

AI "won't tell us what to build, and it isn't responsible for it," he said.

Retail brokers that announced layoffs this year sized them at no more than a tenth of their workforce, and AI featured in at least two of the explanations.

eToro cut about 7% of its global staff in January, and IronFX cut about 150 of its roughly 1,500 jobs in March. eToro said it was using process automation and AI to operate more efficiently, while sources cited efficiency amid the AI wave at IronFX.

FP Markets reduced its global workforce by less than 7% in April. By FinanceMagnates.com's calculation, FTMO's plan would add about three times as many people, relative to the group's size, as IronFX removed.

OANDA Takes Half the New Roles

Half of the hiring targets OANDA, where the founders have already changed the management since the takeover.

Vašíček and co-founder Otakar Šuffner have run OANDA as co-CEOs since Gavin Bambury stepped down in March. Vašíček said they parted ways with several people after the takeover and are now strengthening existing teams.

He also said OANDA does not offer everything it could in many of its markets. Its estimated trading volume fell 10% quarter-over-quarter in the third quarter of 2026, FM Intelligence's broker volumes tracker shows.

AI Spending in the Millions, Listing Not Ruled Out

FTMO is looking for experienced hires, including AI specialists and product engineers who use AI to take a feature from brief to launch, CzechCrunch reported. A two-day sprint at the Prague office replaces the usual three interview rounds, with a decision within 24 hours.

FTMO spends millions of dollars a year on AI and has direct contracts with Anthropic and Google, according to the report. It has automated content, translations and invoicing.

FTMO plans four product launches next year and is building out futures, which it opened to traders in beta in August, according to CzechCrunch.

The group reported 2025 revenue of about $420 million, up 31%, while net income fell 59% to roughly $37.5 million, the founders told FinanceMagnates.com in October. In that interview, Šuffner did not rule out a stock market listing.

"An FTMO ticker sounds really cool," he said.

title: Chainlink and Moody’s Complete Testnet Pilot for Cross-Chain Credit Ratings
summary: Chainlink and Moody's tested distribution of credit-rating information across blockchains using representative data, with production deployment still separate.
content:
TL;DR: Chainlink and Moody's Ratings completed a cross-chain distribution pilot using test data. It ran on testnets and did not publish live rating actions or change Moody's existing publication processes.

Tokenized finance needs information to move alongside assets. In a November 10 announcement, Chainlink and Moody's Ratings reported a completed pilot that used the Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol, or CCIP, to distribute credit information across multiple networks.

The exercise connected Moody's Token Integration Engine, known as TIE, with cross-chain messaging. Its significance lies in a familiar market problem: investors need consistent information about an instrument even when different pieces of financial infrastructure represent or hold it.

A ratings-distribution test with defined limits

The pilot used representative data in a controlled testnet environment, spanning permissioned and permissionless networks. No actual rating actions were published onchain, and live dissemination processes were not involved.

That scope makes the result useful as an interoperability test. It leaves the separate work of operating a production service, setting responsibilities and integrating it with financial institutions.

Consider a hypothetical bond represented across several networks. If its credit assessment changes, a reliable system needs to identify the relevant instrument and ensure each destination receives the appropriate update. Otherwise, applications can act on different versions of information about the same underlying obligation.

CCIP carries messages as well as tokens

Chainlink's documentation describes CCIP as infrastructure for transferring both data and tokens between blockchains. Its developer tools cover standalone messages and transactions that combine value transfers with instructions.

This matters because a rating update is information. Delivering it does not necessarily require moving the asset itself. A recipient application can receive a message and decide how to use it according to its own rules and permissions.

The documentation also includes message-status, execution and finality tools. Those operational details become important when a financial workflow needs to determine whether an update has arrived, whether it has been processed and how to handle an exception.

NewsBTC has examined the configurable controls around this infrastructure in its report on CCIP 2.0's security and compliance features.

Moody's had already begun integrating ratings onchain

The new test sits within a longer programme. In June, Moody's announced an Alphaledger integration for Solana, giving issuers on that platform an option to integrate ratings with tokenized fixed-income assets. That followed TIE's March deployment on Canton.

Moody's described TIE as network-agnostic. The aim is to make its analytical information available within different blockchain environments, with the underlying credit opinion retaining its established role.

This history is useful because connecting a ratings service to one network and distributing information across several networks are related but separate tasks. The latest pilot tests a way to extend that reach; it should not be presented as the first time Moody's explored blockchain delivery.

Production success will depend on information quality

Our assessment is that the hardest questions extend beyond whether a message can cross a network boundary. A production workflow needs clear instrument identifiers, controls over who can publish updates, a record of changes and rules for handling delayed or disputed information.

It also needs to preserve the meaning of the data. A credit rating is an analytical opinion about credit risk. Putting that opinion onchain does not make an asset risk-free or remove the need to assess its liquidity, price and legal terms.

Similar lifecycle work appears in NewsBTC's coverage of Chainlink's tokenized-equity dividend demonstration. A ledger can carry an asset, but the asset's obligations and information still need maintenance.

The pilot offers evidence that one distribution route can work in a test setting. Named production integrations, defined update policies and operating records would provide the next evidence of how it performs for real portfolios.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Helius Launches Solana Privacy Rings With Confidential Balances and Transfers
summary: Helius has launched Solana Privacy Rings on mainnet, introducing confidential transfers while leaving addresses visible in the default ring.
content:
TL;DR: Helius launched Solana Privacy Rings on mainnet on November 10. The default ring hides assets and amounts within private transfers, while sender and recipient addresses remain visible.

Solana applications have a new way to offer confidential balances. Helius's launch announcement introduces Privacy Rings as programmable pools that execute on Solana, giving developers tools for private payments and financial applications on the same network.

The feature addresses a practical obstacle for public-ledger payments. A business may want the settlement benefits of a blockchain without publishing every payment amount to competitors or employees. Individual users can have similar concerns about exposing the size and history of their financial activity.

Confidentiality has a specific boundary

The technical documentation separates confidentiality from anonymity. In the default confidential ring, assets, amounts and optional memos are encrypted during private transfers, while the participating wallet addresses remain public. A visible transaction hash also remains part of the record.

Entering from a public balance has a different footprint: the deposit's asset, amount and addresses are visible, even though the resulting private balance is encrypted. Users should therefore understand each step of a payment, rather than assume that selecting a private balance hides all earlier activity.

This is a meaningful improvement for applications that mainly need to conceal amounts. It also establishes a clear limit: a counterparty relationship can still be observable. Product designers will need to explain that distinction before users rely on it.

Privacy becomes part of application design

Helius says developers can integrate the system through APIs and build private escrows for financial activity. Its planned uses include confidential swaps, staking and yield-related applications. The launch provides a foundation that other teams can incorporate into their products.

Our reading is that the integration experience will matter as much as the cryptography. A useful payment screen must tell a user which information is exposed, how to review a transaction and what happens if an application stops working. Privacy that is difficult to understand can create expectations the software does not meet.

The broader usability question also appears in NewsBTC's reporting on Samsung Wallet's live USDC rollout on Solana. Reaching users requires a workable product around the underlying network capability.

Enterprise rings remain a separate release

The Solana Foundation's account of the launch describes Custom Rings as an upcoming product in audit. Those environments are intended to give institutions configurable privacy, auditor access and controls such as eligibility restrictions.

The foundation says the enterprise version is expected in the coming weeks. That expectation should be tracked as a delivery milestone. The current permissionless launch and the planned enterprise release have different operating requirements.

For an institution, confidentiality is only one part of the problem. Staff still need appropriate access, auditors need reliable evidence, and a payment's legal and accounting treatment must remain clear. NewsBTC's coverage of Solana's delivery-versus-payment programme examines another piece of that wider settlement workflow.

Security review and adoption are ongoing tests

The foundation reports audits of the core programmes and proof circuits by Certora, OtterSec and ZK Security, while formal verification is still underway. It also identifies applications and service providers working with the infrastructure. These are useful implementation details, with separate questions still open about usage and long-term reliability.

An audit evaluates a defined version and scope; it cannot establish that every future integration handles keys, permissions and disclosures correctly. Developers adding privacy features inherit their own responsibility for the surrounding application.

The next useful evidence will be applications people can repeatedly use, clear documentation of their privacy boundaries and sustained security review. The launch makes confidential activity more accessible on Solana, while the quality of each integration will determine how much protection a user actually receives.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Aave Proposal Targets $3.5M in Added Annual Revenue Through Reserve-Factor Changes
summary: TokenLogic proposes reserve-factor changes across Aave markets, with an estimated $3.5 million annual revenue increase at a fixed snapshot.
content:
TL;DR: TokenLogic proposes changes to Aave's reserve factors across 54 reserves. Its model estimates $3.5 million in additional annual revenue, using November 9 balances and rates; governance has not yet approved the changes.

Aave's latest revenue proposal focuses on how lending income is divided. A November 12 submission from TokenLogic covers 12 V3 instances and V2 Ethereum, with the modeled blended reserve factor rising from 12.0% to 12.7%.

The practical issue is straightforward: the protocol treasury would retain a larger share of interest, leaving a smaller share for suppliers where a change applies. Whether that improves the economics over time depends partly on how those suppliers respond.

What the reserve factor controls

Aave's official FAQ defines the reserve factor as the percentage of borrowing interest that accrues to the treasury. It is set for each asset through governance. The treasury is controlled by Aave Governance, rather than functioning as a conventional company's bank account.

A simplified example makes the mechanism clearer. Suppose borrowers generate $100 of interest and a reserve factor is 20%. Before considering other mechanics, $20 goes to the treasury and $80 remains for suppliers. Raising the factor to 25% changes that split to $25 and $75. The underlying $100 of interest has not grown simply because the allocation changed.

This hypothetical illustrates why a higher reserve factor can improve treasury receipts while reducing the attractiveness of supplying to the same market. It also shows why the percentage should not be read as an annual return paid to either group.

Suppliers face different effects across markets

TokenLogic proposes moving Ethereum Core DAI's factor from 25% to 30%, while Avalanche V3 USDC would move from 10% to 25%. The proposal's stated purpose includes changing incentives across legacy markets as Aave's newer infrastructure develops.

The immediate parameter change does not itself alter the borrower interest rate. Over time, however, a supplier response could change available liquidity and utilisation. Those subsequent effects make it important to distinguish a mechanical estimate from a forecast of the eventual outcome.

NewsBTC's report on Aave's externally curated V4 markets offers context on how the protocol is developing different arrangements for managing liquidity and risk.

V4 provides a different destination for activity

Aave's official protocol changelog records the launch of V4 on Ethereum in March and on Avalanche in July. The architecture groups liquidity into hubs and lending activity into separate spokes, giving the network a different way to organise markets.

That deployment history helps explain why comparisons between versions now matter commercially. A supplier considering a change in yield can compare not only competing protocols but also different Aave deployments, with their own assets, liquidity conditions and operational characteristics.

Our reading is that governance is making an allocation decision about where activity should be encouraged. That deserves scrutiny at the individual-market level: a portfolio-wide revenue estimate can hide quite different experiences for suppliers of different assets.

The estimate still has to survive market behaviour

The revenue figure annualises a snapshot. Borrowed balances can rise or fall, interest rates can change, and liquidity can move after a parameter update. The estimate therefore gives a basis for comparison, while the realised result remains open.

Governance also has to consider the cost of retaining liquidity and the resilience of each market. An extra dollar of treasury income is less useful if the settings create an offsetting loss of activity or a more fragile funding base.

Interest in AAVE ownership, including Payward's recently disclosed investment, makes these economic decisions relevant to a wider audience. The next steps are community feedback and an onchain proposal, followed by measurable results if the changes are approved and executed.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Solana Company Reports $3.4M Quarterly Revenue as Staking Business Expands
summary: Solana Company reported $3.4 million in third-quarter revenue as its treasury staking and Asia-Pacific validator infrastructure developed.
content:
TL;DR: Solana Company reported $3.4 million in third-quarter revenue, mostly from staking. Its results show how validator operations can add an operating business to a corporate SOL treasury.

Solana Company is beginning to report more of the economics behind its infrastructure strategy. In its November 11 earnings release, the Nasdaq-listed company said revenue reached $3.4 million in the quarter ended September 30, compared with $697,000 a year earlier.

The question for shareholders is how much of that business can grow beyond the size of the company's own token holdings. A balance sheet gives exposure to SOL; an operating validator business adds a different set of customers, costs and performance measures.

Treasury rewards and outside delegations

The company reported approximately 2.4 million SOL across its holdings categories at quarter-end. It earned 30,800 SOL in quarterly staking rewards and restaked them. Its Pacific Backbone infrastructure had about 1.3 million SOL delegated, including roughly one million from third parties.

Those figures describe different relationships with tokens. Treasury assets belong to the company, while third-party delegations represent outside stake using its infrastructure. Combining the two into a single ownership figure would overstate the company's treasury.

NewsBTC's coverage of DeFi Development Corp's SOL accumulation provides useful context on the distinction between growing a token balance and creating value for each share.

Pacific Backbone was designed as an operating expansion

The company's February infrastructure roadmap set out plans to connect Seoul, Tokyo, Singapore and Hong Kong through a low-latency validator network. Its intended customers included trading firms, exchanges and institutional partners.

The stated business logic was to bring more infrastructure work in-house while developing services that outside customers could use. That provides a useful baseline for judging the latest update: the original plan involved building an activity that could generate fees as well as supporting treasury staking.

The programme also envisaged additional liquidity and execution services. Those earlier ambitions should be assessed separately from what subsequent financial reports demonstrate. A roadmap is useful for tracking delivery, but it cannot substitute for revenue, customers and operating margins.

Why delegated stake can generate income

Solana's official staking documentation explains that token holders delegate stake to validators that process transactions and participate in running the network. Validators may retain a commission from rewards to cover their work and costs.

This structure creates two routes to an operating benefit. A company can earn rewards on its own delegated tokens, and a validator operator can earn commissions for serving other holders. The economics depend on performance, expenses and the amount of stake retained.

The documentation also makes a useful accounting distinction: staking increases are measured in SOL units. Their value in dollars moves with SOL's market price. More tokens therefore do not automatically mean a higher fiat value at the end of a reporting period.

The equity case needs more than token growth

Our assessment is that third-party delegation makes the business more interesting to analyse, because it introduces demand from customers outside the treasury. It also makes the reporting more demanding. Investors need to distinguish rewards earned on company assets from fees earned on client stake and then compare both with operating costs.

Capital structure remains important. Issuing shares can expand a treasury while changing the amount of token exposure attributable to each shareholder. Cash expenses can also require financing even when reported token holdings rise.

Custody and access are additional parts of the picture, as NewsBTC examined in Solmate's disclosure of its SOL custody arrangements. Subsequent reports showing delegation retention, fee income and cash expenditure will help establish whether Solana Company's infrastructure adds durable earnings alongside its asset exposure.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: BTSE Enterprise Solutions Wins Best White-Label Digital Asset Exchange Platform at Digital Banker Awards 2026
summary: Apia, Samoa, 13th November 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Apia, Samoa, 13th November 2026, Chainwire

Apia, Samoa, November 13th, 2026, Chainwire

BTSE Enterprise Solutions has been named Best White-Label Digital Asset Exchange Platform by a Vendor at the Digital Banker Awards 2026. The awards are presented by The Digital Banker, a global financial media and research platform known for its banking awards programs, which recognize leading banks, financial institutions and technology providers worldwide. 

The Digital Banker’s audience is senior decision-makers across banking and financial technology, including executives at banks, payment providers and digital asset businesses. Its awards are designed to serve as unbiased benchmarks for the industry, giving institutions an independent signal when choosing partners. For brokers and trading platforms weighing a digital asset launch, that matters: the choice of vendor is often what determines whether a project clears licensing, due diligence and board approval.

BTSE Enterprise Solutions offers a white-label platform that lets partners launch a branded exchange in weeks rather than years. Each deployment can be configured to support jurisdiction-specific requirements, helping operators address local requirements without rebuilding the core platform. More than 100 corporate clients now run exchange and payment platforms with BTSE Enterprise Solutions.

“Companies entering digital assets aren’t just looking for a vendor. They’re looking for an operator they can trust from day one,” said Jeff Mei, COO of BTSE Enterprise Solutions. “And most of our clients don’t come to us for just software. They come because running an exchange safely at scale is hard. Not only do they need around-the-clock technical and operations support, but they also need a partner that can provide a strategic view of their business and how it fits within the industry as a whole.” Mei said the award belongs to the company’s engineers and operations personnel, and to every client who trusted BTSE with their brand.

Looking ahead, BTSE is focused on helping traditional financial institutions in emerging markets enter digital assets with confidence, and on extending its payments and card products. Regulatory readiness is also becoming a larger part of the business as more countries introduce crypto exchange and payment regulations.

About BTSE Enterprise Solutions

BTSE Enterprise Solutions offers technology solutions under BTSE Group, providing white-label exchange, payments and digital asset infrastructure to banks, fintech companies, brokers and entrepreneurs worldwide. Built on the trading systems expertise behind BTSE’s exchange, the company has offered its enterprise platform since 2022. For more information, visit www.btsesolutions.com.
